title: The dashboard HTML has no data; content waits for hydration and then for /api/runs
summary: The route has no loader: the server renders only "Checking access and loading runs…" and the client fetches /api/runs after hydration (dev: request starts at ~235 ms, content = hydration + API + ~30 ms).

title: Header navigation reloads the whole document, although both lists are already in memory
summary: app-shell.tsx:52-57 renders NavLink with a plain href, so queue/history/status clicks load a new document and refetch /api/runs; the in-page router Link to history makes no request.

title: "Refresh runs" blanks the page and three header items, and reloads the alerts
summary: refresh() sets state to loading (index.tsx:242-245): list, title, repository, bell, and account menu disappear, scroll and history filters reset, and /api/operations loads again (1 -> 2).

title: /api/operations waits for /api/runs, and the service view loads runs that it does not use
summary: OperationsAttention mounts only in the ready state (index.tsx:254-256, 363-364): two authenticated requests in sequence, each with a session read and an account read (at least 6 D1 round trips per load).

title: Pull request titles are erased when the webhook is processed, so the queue shows "Pull request" as the title
summary: dashboard.ts:57-62 reads the title from github_webhook_delivery.payload_json, but webhooks.ts:330-335 sets payload_json='{}' on every processed delivery; after that the lookup matches 0 rows (reproduced in sqlite, production not read).

title: ak-ink-danger, ak-ink-warning, and ak-ink-success do not exist; errors and status icons have no color
summary: ak-ink-* accepts only numbers; six uses (index.tsx:271,331,531, user-menu.tsx:66, operations-attention 370,501) emit no CSS, so error text and icons render in the body color.

title: $layer="primary" is not a recipe color; the main buttons paint a fixed pale gray in both schemes
summary: COLOR_VALUES has no "primary"; the buttons get --layer-color: primary and compute to oklch(0.95 0 0) in dark and light, so the main action is a pale gray box in light mode (review workspace uses "brand").

title: Review cards are 240 px tall; a queue of 40 runs is 8.5 screens long
summary: Each run is a 240-272 px card for five facts; the first card starts at y=361 of 900 (y=398 of 844 on a phone); 40 actionable runs are 7,608 px on desktop and 9,245 px on a phone; the actionable query has no limit.

title: The same facts are stated two to five times; most words on screen can go
summary: Queue with one run: 55 words, about 18 carry data; run count 3x, run state 3x per card, repository 2-3x, "nothing to do" 5x, history scope 3x; the report lists each removable text.

title: Failed and stale runs are at the bottom, with a clock icon and no color
summary: "Needs attention" renders last (index.tsx:542-543) with the same Clock3Icon and gray text as "In progress"; with 40 runs it starts at about y=6,540 of 7,608.

title: Eight run states share four looks, and the same badge has two shapes
summary: needs-review, comparing, and incomplete are all yellow with a clock; failed, rejected, and needs-recompare are all red; the fixture state "reviewing" is gray; the badge is a pill in cards and has a 2 px radius in the table.

title: Only 1.7% of a review card is clickable; history rows link the text block only; link names repeat
summary: Card 1120x240 with one 142x33 link; history link covers 36% of the row; tab order reads "Review changes" x4 and "Open run" x4; time elements have no dateTime.

title: Runs without a title print the kind twice; the icon is always a pull request; nothing links to GitHub
summary: A main run shows "Main" as label and as title with a pull-request icon; PR number and commit are plain text; commit is 12 characters; "Attempt 1" and the year always show.

title: Copy defects: wrong plural, wrong claim for a first-time visitor, lost server message, error far from its button
summary: "1 view await approval."; every 403 says "Your repository access changed"; non-OK answers drop the server message and reference; the sign-in error renders at x=160,y=69 while the button is at x=774,y=363.

title: The sign-in screen is a marketing page for one button
summary: 34 words, two headings, and two paragraphs around one action; the repository is not named; the header shows three links that a guest cannot open.

title: "Use another account" probably returns the same account
summary: The button only signs out of Visonaut and the GitHub provider sets no prompt (auth.ts:29-35), so GitHub most probably signs the same user in again; not tested against GitHub.

title: The account menu never shows who is signed in
summary: No caller passes login to UserMenu, so it always says "Account"; identity.login is in scope during /api/runs but is not returned; /api/session and /api/me have no client caller.

title: History: client-side search over 100 rows, explained three times, with a layout that moves with the data
summary: No paging beyond 100 runs; filter options, control width, and table columns depend on the data (table-layout auto); search focus is an underline only; no result count; phone rows are 83-243 px (3 per screen).

title: The run list never updates on its own
summary: The fetch effect depends only on [reload] (index.tsx:176-210); a run that is comparing or capturing stays stale until the maintainer clicks Refresh, while alerts poll every 60 s.

title: The dashboard hand-writes typography, fields, and lists; the matching primitives are not vendored
summary: 38 Text uses (27 with render and type classes), 24 ak-ink-60, 18 raw divs, native input and select in Frame labels, page header block written 3 times, dead classes dashboard/dashboard-main; Heading, Input, List, Link, Separator, Progress, Tooltip, Code are upstream only.

title: Client and server disagree on the run contract; some branches cannot run
summary: index.tsx re-declares DashboardRun with looser types; the actionable fallback to runs is used only by tests; "superseded" in the recovery filter and the "reviewing" label cannot occur in production; comparisonId, snapshotId, promotionId are unused.

title: Sign-in and sign-out code is written three times
summary: index.tsx, runs.$runId.tsx, and pulls.$pullNumber.tsx each carry signIn/signOut with createAuthClient() per click and the same strings; the 403 message is duplicated inside index.tsx.

title: Preview: the notice repeats, and the fixture renders odd values
summary: "Preview fixtures" shows three times plus "Preview account"; the single fixture run shows commit 000000000000, date Jan 1, 1970, and a gray badge for a state that production does not have.

title: Phone layout: squeezed rows, a floating footer link, and one run per screen
summary: At 390 px the in-progress title wraps to four lines beside the Open run button, "View history" is not right-aligned, the history controls wrap by data, and the first run starts at y=398 of 844.

title: The three counters are ambiguous and are not a list for assistive technology
summary: "29 Awaiting approval" names no unit and includes the rejected views; counters are sums over all actionable runs, rendered as spans, and are zero most of the time.

title: Small visual inconsistencies
summary: Button radius 6.5 px against 2 px on one page, error card width follows the message, five card paddings and two radii, a decorative icon box in every row, uneven section gaps, mixed heading punctuation.

title: Difference mode shows the mask alone: no screenshot context and no image boundary
summary: The diff pane renders only the red-on-transparent mask (screenshot-viewer.tsx:242-261), so the reviewer sees red pixels on an empty checkerboard and cannot tell what they belong to.

title: A small change is a few screen pixels, and nothing points to it
summary: A 120 px change is about 5 x 4 screen px in Compare and 56 reddish px in Difference at 1440 x 900; on a 640 x 3200 image it is 4 px; 200% opens at 0,0 with the change off screen; no boxes, no jump to change.

title: Panes do not share pan; zoom, mode, and variant changes lose the inspected place
summary: Each pane keeps its own scroll ref (screenshot-viewer.tsx:35-48): baseline [400,200] vs current [0,0]; 100% to 200% keeps raw offsets; Compare to Difference lands at [0,0]; next variant resets pan but keeps zoom.

title: The image gets about a quarter of the window, and Fit does not fit the visible area
summary: The stage is a fixed h-[min(56vh,650px)] below seven rows of chrome: image starts at y 432 of 900, uses 26% of the window, and its bottom 59 px (138 px at 1280 x 720) sit under the sticky action bar.

title: Comparison techniques that are missing
summary: No overlay or onion skin, swipe, blink, change boxes, synced pan, pixel inspector, device-pixel 1:1, auto zoom to change, free zoom, or drag to pan (model.ts:2-3; drag and Ctrl+wheel measured as no-ops).

title: Arrow keys never pan, there are no zoom keys, and the mouse cannot drag
summary: With the focusable pane focused at 200%, ArrowRight changes the variant and ArrowDown changes the item; +, -, 0 do nothing; pan needs four 25 px buttons per pane (10 tab stops in Compare).

title: Difference says "within the comparison tolerance" for an image whose size changed
summary: Local comparison stores no mask on a size change (png-comparison.ts:64-66, maskExpected false), so screenshot-viewer.tsx:249-253 shows the tolerance sentence next to "100.00% changed · Needs review".

title: Images with different sizes get different scales in Compare, and nothing marks the size change
summary: Each pane fits its own image: 1280 x 720 renders at scale 0.433 next to 1280 x 1600 at 0.293; the only hint is 10 px caption text.

title: Added, removed, and locally matched variants keep the two-pane layout with an empty pane
summary: Pane visibility depends only on the mode (screenshot-viewer.tsx:221, 236): new, removed, and matched-locally variants show a half-empty or fully empty stage, and on a phone the empty pane comes first.

title: Status rows and pan buttons move the image by 9 to 54 px
summary: Stage top is 414 px when ready, 423 zoomed, 439 for added, 455 while loading, 468 on error, because status rows and pan buttons are inserted above the image.

title: No preload and no placeholder: each variant change shows an empty stage until two full images load and decode
summary: Zero requests for the next variant before selection; then 2 image requests (3 in Difference) while the stage is blank; the 256 px thumbnail and known dimensions are not used as a placeholder.

title: The image has no visible boundary, and the checkerboard does not mean transparency
summary: The checkerboard is the background of the whole scroll box and the img has no ring, so light captures merge with the light stage and dark captures with the dark stage.

title: Four vocabularies for the same four views
summary: Buttons say Compare/Difference/Current/Baseline, alt text says Reference/New image/Pixel diff, help and docs say Side by side/New only/Original only, code says side/diff/new/original.

title: Fit never enlarges small images and squeezes tall or wide images; zoom has three fixed levels
summary: A 32 x 32 capture stays 32 x 32 in a 591 x 504 pane; a 640 x 3200 capture becomes a 94 px strip; only Fit, 100%, 200% exist, with no fit-width and no device-pixel 1:1.

title: Phone layout: the first image starts at 63% of the screen, and the two images are never visible together
summary: At 390 x 844 the baseline image starts at y 535 and the current image 522 px lower; the mode group overflows (401 vs 366 px) and controls are 25 px tall.

title: The disabled Approve button looks enabled while images load or fail
summary: While evidence loads the brand button is disabled but keeps the same background and opacity 1; only the label drops to 73% alpha (cross-lane with the action bar).

title: Accessible names and roles in the viewer
summary: Focusable scroll region has aria-label but no role; mode names include the shortcut letter ("Compare S") with no aria-keyshortcuts; pan label and title differ; exclusive modes use aria-pressed toggles.

title: View state is not shareable and not remembered
summary: Mode and zoom are plain useState (review-workspace.tsx:197-198): a reload returns to Compare at Fit and a link cannot carry view, zoom, or position.

title: The viewer goes around the primitives, and its class hooks have no styles
summary: Raw text sizes (10 to 13 px), title tooltips, plain status divs, and a 170 character background class; review-* classes have no CSS and exist only for tests; upstream Tooltip, Progress, Separator are not vendored.

title: Small text and state defects around the viewer
summary: "0.00% changed · 1 changed pixels", "— changed pixels", an announcement that contradicts the visible hint, Difference enabled with nothing to show, recovery buttons that look like text, stale pan after Retry (code only).

title: The review page gives the screenshots less than a third of the viewport
summary: At 1440x900 the first image pixel is at y=449 and the visible image area is 29.7% of the viewport (24.7% at 1920x1080); seven chrome rows and a min(56vh,650px) pane cap come first, while Percy and Argos use a viewer-first workspace.

title: The viewer cannot overlay, swipe, or blink the two images
summary: ReviewMode is side | diff | new | original; GitHub, Playwright, reg-cli, Chromatic, Percy, and Argos all offer overlay, slider, or toggle modes, and the stored diff is already a transparent pixelmatch mask so these need no backend change.

title: Zoomed panes scroll separately, so a zoomed comparison shows two different regions
summary: After two pan clicks at 200% the baseline pane is at scrollLeft 296, scrollTop 252 and the current pane stays at 0,0; each pane owns its scroll state and there is no drag or wheel zoom, while Argos keeps zoom and pan in sync.

title: Nothing shows where the change is inside the image
summary: The page prints only a ratio and a pixel count (for example 0.05%, 120 pixels) and no code reads the mask; Percy, Argos, Chromatic, and reg-cli highlight changed regions and step through them.

title: The variant strip hides the verdict and holds three variants
summary: Three of seven variant pills fit at 1440 wide (content 2079 px in a 1120 px strip), approved pills look like pending pills because VariantSummary renders no status, and every pill repeats the shared axis text.

title: The queue uses a 240 px card for 22 words and states each count three times
summary: Queue cards are 240 px high with 21 to 24 words and start at y=361, so two fit at 1440x900, while the history table shows the same runs in 64 px rows; Argos and Graphite use dense rows in sections.

title: The dashboard has no keyboard flow
summary: No key handler exists in routes/index.tsx or the pull route, and the run page has no key to return to the queue or open the next run; Linear, GitHub, Graphite, and Chromatic connect list and detail with keys.

title: One decision stops at one item, and equal diffs are not grouped
summary: The widest decision scope is all changed variants of one item behind a confirmation dialog; Percy has snapshot, matching-diff group, and build scopes and Chromatic has accept all, with public demand and a documented risk on both sides.

title: The item list cannot sort by change size or filter by kind or axis
summary: Items keep the declared order and the filter has four status values, although ratio and changedPixels are in the model; Argos shipped sort by change size after a 248-file build report and Percy sorts by diff percent.

title: The run page states the review status four times
summary: Sidebar text, header text, identity row text, and a badge all say needs review, plus a dot and a progress bar; the page shows 97 words and 26 controls for a one-item run, where Argos uses one progress chip.

title: Three vocabularies name the same four image modes, and the guide uses labels that the UI does not have
summary: Buttons say Compare, Difference, Current, Baseline; accessible names say Reference, New image, Pixel diff; the guide says Side by side, Pixel diff, New only, Original only, and All runs where the UI says Queue.

title: The ? key does not open the shortcut list, and its button is below the fold
summary: The Keyboard help button sits at y=985 to 996 in a 900 px viewport and the key handler has no ? branch; Argos opens the full shortcut list with ?.

title: A rejection has no reason, and there is no place for a note
summary: ReviewCommand carries a verdict and targets only; Percy writes a comment on a change request and Argos, Chromatic, and Vercel pin comments to the pixel, so the reason for a rejection must travel through another channel.

title: Noise has no verdict of its own
summary: The verdict type is approved or rejected only; Argos (ignore and auto-ignore), Chromatic (ignore, flake filter, quarantine), and Happo (report flake) all added a third channel for diffs that the change did not cause.

title: `$layer="primary"` is not a recipe color; six primary surfaces including both sign-in buttons render neutral gray
summary: routes/index.tsx:301,310,346,508 and routes/pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:194,226 pass "primary"; the recipe knows only canvas/brand/secondary/success/warning/danger, so it emits inline `--layer-color: primary` and the computed background is rgb(238,238,238) in both schemes instead of brand rgb(0,106,187). A third sign-in button (runs.$runId.tsx:236) has no layer at all.

title: Four review banners use `ak-layer-warning` without `ak-layer` and paint no surface; warnings have three looks
summary:
review/review-workspace.tsx:690,695,701,706 use `

`; computed background is rgba(0,0,0,0) in dark and light, so a role=alert run error looks like body text. The pull page paints a solid yellow Frame and badges use a tint.

title: Selection is hand-rolled with `$lighten`; the selected sidebar row and variant chip are not visible in the light scheme
summary: item-list.tsx:199-202 and review-workspace.tsx:719-739 set `$selectedPush={false}` plus `$lighten={2}`; measured selected rgb(254,255,255) on rgb(252,253,253) = 1.017:1 in light (1.258:1 in dark), and the selected chip has no ring while unselected chips have one. The top nav with recipe defaults is visible in both schemes.

title: Nested frames lose their radius: square buttons, tiles, badges, and cards in five places
summary: Computed border-radius is 2px for Approve/Reject (review-workspace.tsx:1062-1097), "Open run" and clock tiles (index.tsx:580-597), table status badges (index.tsx:725-727), and popover alert cards and guide button, while the same components measure 6.5px, 7px, 10.5px, or full pill elsewhere. Upstream sandbox uses `$forceRounded` for badges in table cells.

title: Text is muted with `opacity-*` in 13 places; two measured cases fail WCAG AA in the light scheme
summary: `opacity-50` on the 10px run meta strip (review-workspace.tsx:610) and the 11px item count (:551) measures 3.96:1 in light; `ak-ink-40/50` text of the same size measures 4.59:1 because ink keeps the AA floor.

title: A disabled brand button keeps its full brand fill; "Approve & next" looks active on read-only runs
summary: With `archived: true` the approve button has disabled=true but background stays rgb(0,106,187); only label alpha drops to 0.73. Cause is in the vendored control recipe (`bg-none!` removes images, not the layer color); same classes at upstream HEAD, not browser-verified there.

title: `Text` is used 79 times but only once with a text variant; typography is 48 ad-hoc class sets and 13 font sizes
summary: Text recipe is only a marker class plus `$text*` color variants, so 72 uses pass only className; eyebrow labels have 3 spellings, page titles 5, and sizes run 10/11/12/13/14/16/18/20/24/28/30/36/48px. Upstream Heading and Prose are not vendored.

title: Fourteen upstream primitives are not vendored; the app hand-rolls an equivalent for ten of them
summary: Missing: checkbox, code, combobox, dialog, heading, input, link, list, option, progress, prose, radio, separator, tooltip. Hand-rolled: 4 dialogs, raw input and select, a 10-part tag-combobox, raw progress, 5 separators, 14 title tooltips, 4 raw code, 3 raw links, 2 dl lists. Report has a 21-row need/current/primitive/rewrite table.

title: Four hand-rolled dialogs have three different looks; the keyboard-help dialog has an unstyled heading
summary: review-workspace.tsx:155-186, 1206-1222, 1223-1241, 1242-1296 each set their own position math, radius (lg vs 2xl), padding (5 vs 6), and heading class (none vs text-lg font-semibold); the `bg-black/50!` backdrop Layer is copied 4 times.

title: Vendored `Kbd` and `Tabs` have zero importers and add about 10% to the stylesheet; Disclosure, PopoverScroll, ShellFooter parts, ButtonSeparator are bypassed
summary: In-memory Tailwind compile: 371,158 bytes with all sources, 332,500 without tabs+kbd (−10.4%, −5,364 gzip). The app uses native details, hand-rolled scroll boxes, and plain-text key lists where the vendored primitives exist.

title: `ControlButton` is imported as `Button`, the real `Button` as `FlatButton`, and font size is overridden by class 18 times
summary: control-button.tsx:4-13 adds `$rounded="lg" $p={2.5} text-[13px] leading-5` (and restates the default `$kind="flat"`); five files alias it to `Button`; its defaults are copied by hand in three other components; `$size` is used once while `className="text-xs"` is used 15 times. Upstream Button now accepts a `recipe` prop for this.

title: Eighteen `!important` overrides and repeated internal custom properties fight the Shell and Nav recipes
summary: 10 of the 18 are in review-workspace.tsx (ShellSidebarBody `overflow-hidden! pt-0!`, ShellMainIntro `py-0!`, ShellMainBody `pb-0!`, ShellFooter `flex! min-h-10!`); `[--shell-header-step:calc(48px/14)]` is repeated in 4 files; `border-(--ak-edge)` is read directly 5 times; item-list wraps ak.CompositeItem in NavLink with `item={false} role={undefined}`.

title: Surfaces: 26 prop sets for 33 Frame uses, six card variants, and raised cards that do not separate from the light canvas
summary: Card padding steps 4/5/6/7/8 and radii lg/xl/2xl are mixed; in light a `$lighten` card is rgb(254,255,255) on canvas rgb(252,253,253) (canvas L=99.33%), so only the 1px ring separates it; `$darken={3}` icon tiles are pure black in dark and mid gray in light.

title: Status has four renderings and two vocabularies; the preview state `reviewing` has a label but no color
summary: RunStatus badge (index.tsx:383), ReviewStatus badge (review-status.tsx), sidebar dot (item-list.tsx:270), and RunGroup rows that always show a clock icon (index.tsx:580); labels differ between index.tsx:130-140 and use-review-session.ts:57-80; stateColor lacks `reviewing` which preview-fixtures.ts:84 sends.

title: The vendored copy is restructured and reformatted, so a refresh cannot be a file copy; upstream has 13 newer commits with API changes
summary: Content equals pin fc85b809 (0 differing lines in a line-set comparison) but 9 recipes are inlined into component files with 5 one-line adapter files; diff against the formatted pin is 4,140 lines in 17 files. Upstream since the pin: +790 −279, NavIcon → NavSlot, Button `recipe` prop, BadgeLabel recipe, slot and text-frame changes.

title: The theme names "Inter Variable" as the first font but the app ships no font
summary: ui.css:12-14 declares "Inter Variable"; no @font-face or font package exists; document.fonts is empty and CDP reports the h1 rendered in `.SF NS`, so metrics differ by platform.

title: Stylesheet and DOM weight of the primitive layer: 59 KB gzip CSS and about 1.6 KB of class names per control
summary: Existing dist CSS is 464,666 bytes raw / 59,384 gzip / 32,868 brotli and about 79% of unminified CSS comes from recipes; the workspace DOM has 153,129 characters of class attributes in 248,154 characters of body HTML. Minor next to 101 KB gzip of entry JS; the size is not the cause of slow loads. The work that the rules give to the browser for each element is a cost in a session: see PERF-01, PERF-03, PERF-05, and PERF-07.

title: 34 marker classes have no CSS rule, 15 have no consumer, and `review.css` holds no review styles
summary: Classes such as `review-result`, `dashboard-main`, `review-view-controls` match no CSS, no source selector, and no test; 16 others are test hooks only. review.css is two imports and is imported from four places.

title: Horizontal strips overflow without any sign: 7 variants need 2,079px in a 1,120px strip
summary: `.review-variants` has clientWidth 1120, scrollWidth 2079, overflow-x auto and no scrollbar, fade, or count; each chip repeats shared parts ("Chromium · Light · 1280 × 720"); on a 390px phone the view switch is cut at "Baselir"; number keys cover only variants 1-6.

title: The hand-rolled history search shows keyboard focus only as a text underline; the select draws its ring inside the field border
summary: routes/index.tsx:656-662 uses `outline-none focus-visible:underline` on a raw input inside a Frame label; measured outline none with only text-decoration underline on focus, wrapper unchanged. Three fields use three focus styles; upstream InputGroup handles the group ring.

title: Every production run page shows a disabled "Recompare stored run" button and a 20-word pipeline sentence
summary: The server always sends recompareAllowed: false plus a reason (api/review.ts:592-598), so the footer always renders a dead button and the sentence "Run trusted Submit again from the complete CI bundle…" (review-workspace.tsx:1186-1201).

title: One concept has two to five names
summary: view/variant/item/screenshot/capture, Baseline/Reference/original, Current/New image/candidate, Compare/Side by side, decision/command, and images/evidence are mixed across labels, accessible names, help text, save messages, and docs.

title: The same run status has two or three different labels
summary: Eight server states map to 20 labels through stateLabel (routes/index.tsx:130-140), runStatusLabel (use-review-session.ts:57-80), viewer titles (review-workspace.tsx:956-964), and the pull request page.

title: Variant labels repeat every part, and the accessible name is a raw token string
summary: The consumer key joins framework, project, viewport, style, scheme, contrast, and forced colors, and the pill prints it after the icons: pills measure 390-413 px, 2 of 7 fit in 1,120 px, and the name is "1. react · chromium · light · no-preference · none · react-chrome-default-…. Needs review".

title: The workspace puts seven text bands above the image and repeats the review state six times
summary: The image starts at 408 px of 900 (45%) on desktop and 518 px of 844 (61%) on mobile, and "need(s) review" occurs 6 times in the default state (13 in the batch dialog).

title: The queue and history pages state each fact two or three times
summary: Repository twice, ready count three times, the 100-run limit three times, "Attempt N" on every row (6 and 20 times), "Baseline revision 27", and a duplicate "View history" link; six runs need a 1,515 px page.

title: Count strings have grammar and placeholder defects
summary: "1 view await approval." (index.tsx:502), "All 1 changed views…" (review-workspace.tsx:1055), "— changed pixels" (:647), "Color threshold 0.2; " with a trailing separator (api/review.ts:525), and "Comparison N" that is the run revision (2 becomes 4 after one save).

title: Empty image panes and the pixel-diff hint make false or unneeded statements
summary: The Baseline pane always says "New image, no reference" when the image is null, also beside the error "Required reference evidence is unavailable", and "Pixel diff requires both a reference and a new image." shows on every addition and removal.

title: Three sign-in texts, three access-denied texts, three loading texts
summary: Each route has its own gate copy; the dashboard uses a five-block marketing hero, the run page names "Ariakit" and offers only Retry on HTTP 403, a first 403 says "Your repository access changed.", and loading text names the access check.

title: Error prefixes mislabel server responses, and one user message never arrives
summary: The client marks every HTTP 409 as "Conflict." (client.ts:274-276) although the server uses 409 for expired sessions, closed history, and missing records; HTTP 401 on save renders "Not saved. Sign in with GitHub." with no sign-in control; review-queue.ts:37 throws a plain Error that becomes the generic 503 text.

title: Pipeline and storage words reach the reviewer
summary: Attempt, Baseline revision, Comparison N, sealed, trusted Submit, CI bundle, promoted history, image bytes, evidence (17 strings), and sha256 digests in the details panel are printed without translation to the review task.

title: The service status copy has five names for the feature and operator runbook text in every alert
summary: Operations, Service status, Service attention, operation alerts, and service alerts name one feature; the surface holds 596 of 2,256 client words (26%), with 15 alert bodies of 12 to 33 words and five sentences about its own mechanics.

title: Accessible names differ from visible labels, and shortcut letters are part of button names
summary: Captions say Baseline/Current/Difference while alt text says Reference/New image/Pixel diff; a pan button has aria-label "Pan Reference left" and title "Pan baseline left"; button names are "Approve & nextA" and "Compare S"; the Screenshots sidebar is named "Review navigation" and "Review items".

title: Heading punctuation and capitalization are inconsistent
summary: 11 headings end with a period ("Your review queue.") and the others do not; labels mix "Retry Undo", "fresh Submit", and "Approve & next"; five different retry phrasings exist.

title: The UI does not say who is signed in or which run a tab holds
summary: No caller passes login to UserMenu, so it always shows "Account" with "Manage your GitHub session."; the tab title is always "Visonaut"; conflict text prints the numeric GitHub user ID.

title: The preview shows dates from 1969 and says "Preview fixtures" four times on one screen
summary: preview-fixtures.ts uses createdAt: 0 and checkedAt: 0, so the public preview renders "Dec 31, 1969, 9:00 PM", and the fixture label is used as repository name, eyebrow, notice, and account label.

title: The review guide names controls that the UI does not have
summary: docs/review-guide.md uses "Side by side", "Pixel diff", "New only", "Original only", "All runs", "Retry", and "The Runs page", and says Recompare is retired, while the UI shows Compare, Difference, Current, Baseline, Queue, Retry images, and the Recompare button.

title: Twelve strings cannot be shown by the production code path
summary: The recompare flow messages, two client fallbacks that the server always overrides, the noop message (no code sets noop), "@{login}", and three server recompare errors are unreachable from the UI.

title: Header links, the brand link, and the "Queue" button reload the whole document
summary: app-shell.tsx:16-18,29,53-58 and review-workspace.tsx:580 use plain <a href>; each header click loads a new document and refetches /api/runs, while the in-page <Link> to history costs zero requests.

title: No page ships data from the server, and each mount starts again with "Checking access…"
summary: Server HTML holds only loading text (index.tsx:161,176-184; runs.$runId.tsx:31-36 ssr:false, gcTime:0); the API call starts after hydration, Back remounts and refetches, scroll goes from 250 to 0, and no link preloads.

title: The alerts request waits for the run list, and the Service status page waits for a run list that it does not use
summary: OperationsAttention mounts only when the run list is ready (index.tsx:254-256,356-364); measured /api/operations starts after /api/runs ends on both / and /?view=service.

title: After a click on a run, the old page stays for up to 1 second with no feedback, then the page goes blank
summary: runs.$runId.tsx sets pendingMinMs:0 but no pendingMs, so the 1000 ms router default applies: queue still shown at 152, 501, 902 ms after the click, then a one-line pending page without account menu.

title: The dev stylesheet contains Tailwind and ui.css two times for the root, and four times on the run route
summary: styles.css imports review.css, which imports tailwindcss and ui.css again; dev root CSS is 883,047 B with 2 copies and the run route 1,625,503 B with 4 copies (production build not measured).

title: The review workspace uses 408 px of a 900 px viewport before the first image pixel
summary: App header 48, main header 48, identity strip 26, heading, variant chips, view controls, and captions stack above the image; the image band is 48% of a 1440x900 viewport and 28% of a 390x844 one, with three links to "/".

title: Each page has the document title "Visonaut"
summary: __root.tsx:10 sets the only title; /, history, service, a run, a pull page, and /nope all report "Visonaut".

title: URL model: pages are a search parameter, a pull request link works only with a check ID, and view state is not in the URL
summary: /?view= selects three pages in one 752-line route; /pulls/N without check always 404s (api/review.ts:739-741) and then redirects to a run UUID; the run model has the PR number only inside its title string; mode and zoom are local state.

title: Item and variant links add history entries and scroll the page to the top; keyboard selection replaces the entry
summary: Links in item-list.tsx:205 and review-workspace.tsx:750 push (history 8 to 9 to 10) while navigate uses replace (10 to 10); both reset scrollY from 200 to 0, against 200 to 149 without the router.

title: An unknown URL shows the bare text "Not Found", a missing run offers only "Retry", and the root has no error component
summary:
No notFoundComponent or errorComponent on the root or router; GET /nope returns

Not Found

with no shell, and RunError shows Retry for 404 and 403.

title: With a root font size above 16 px, the item list and the details panel cannot be opened between 1024 px and 64rem
summary: JS uses matchMedia(max-width: 1023px) (review-workspace.tsx:211-213) while CSS uses the 64rem container query ($show="5xl"); at a 20 px root and 1100 px width there is no sidebar, no toggle, no dialog button, and 0 item links.

title: The first Tab stop on a run page is the whole page, and there is no skip link
summary: Shell has tabIndex={0} and aria-label on a div without role (review-workspace.tsx:528-534); first Tab focuses a 1440x994 div with a 1 px edge outline, and nine stops come before main.

title: Small muted text has a 3.96:1 contrast in the light scheme, uses pixel sizes that do not follow the user font size, and is muted in six different ways
summary: text-[10px] opacity-50 on the run identity strip gives 3.96:1 in light (5.34:1 dark); six mute mechanisms (ak-ink-60 x45, opacity-60 x9, opacity-50 x4, ...) and 13 font sizes, 4 of them in px.

title: Sign-in, sign-out, and access errors exist three times, with different layout, copy, and recovery actions
summary: index, runs, and pulls each implement createAuthClient calls (6 sites), a different sign-in card, and different 403 actions; the run 403 state has only Retry and no account menu, and sign-out behaves differently per route.

title: The account menu never shows the signed-in user; the login prop and two identity endpoints have no caller
summary: UserMenu accepts login but no caller passes it, so the label is always "Account"; /api/me (server.ts:88-104) and /api/session (api/review.ts:713-721) have no client call in the repository.

title: There is no layout route; four call sites build their own shell and header, and the header differs between pages
summary: index, pulls, runs, and review-workspace each render Shell plus AppHeader with a repeated --shell-header-step hack; text-sm on one shell shifts the header by 1.5 px, and controls go from 4 to 6 between loading and ready.

title: Keyboard help sits in a page footer below the fold, next to a "Recompare stored run" button that can never be enabled
summary: ShellFooter (review-workspace.tsx:1172-1205) starts at 954 px on a 900 px viewport; the server always sends recompareAllowed:false (api/review.ts:592) and the endpoint always throws, and the guide says the control is retired.

title: One object has several names in the navigation, and the review guide names controls that do not exist
summary: Item is also screenshot and review item, variant is also view and capture, alerts have five names; docs/review-guide.md names a "Runs page" and an "All runs" control that are not in the UI.

title: Shell parts are overridden with ! classes, controls are hand-built where primitives exist, and two vendored components have no user
summary: Four !important overrides on shell parts, native progress, manual separator, four ak.Dialog with manual backdrops, title= tooltips; the vendored copy has 13 components against 27 upstream, and kbd and tabs are unused.

title: Visual details in the shell chrome
summary: Details panel header misaligned by 22 px with the strip, "Accepted" at 16 px beside 12 px rows, 724 px wide flat buttons that look like text, loading text not centered, 1.8 px bold shift on the selected nav link, favicon differs from the header mark.

title: Header controls are smaller than 24 px at a 390 px width, and shortcut letters show on touch layouts
summary: At 390 px the brand link is 19x23 px, the account button 29x29, and the workspace "Queue" link 68x23; key letters show on touch; the guide puts phones outside the launch scope.

title: The sidebar preference script runs in the head of each page, but only a client-only route reads it
summary: __root.tsx:21-26 adds an inline script and suppressHydrationWarning for a value that only the ssr:false workspace reads in a state initializer; no CSS reads the attribute.

title: Shortcuts stop after a mouse click on a variant pill
summary: `.review-variants` is in the shortcut exclusion selector (review-workspace.tsx:94-96), so after a click on a pill A/X/S/D/F/G, arrows and 1-6 do nothing (measured: calls 0, mode stays side, in fixture and routed app).

title: Focus jumps to the page root after each decision and after Undo
summary: `onFocus()` (use-review-session.ts:317, 470) focuses the role-less root `div` (tabIndex 0, aria-label); next Tab goes to the brand link and Approve is 30 Tab presses away; the root is also the first tab stop.

title: Item list unreachable when the px media query and the rem container query disagree
summary: `narrow` uses `(max-width: 1023px)` but the sidebar uses `@5xl/shell` (64rem); with a 20px default font at 1200px, or a 15px scrollbar at 1024-1038px, sidebar, toggle and the Screenshots button are all hidden (0 rows visible).

title: Shift+A and Shift+X skip the confirmation that the button path requires
summary: `Shift+A` saved 7 targets at once with no dialog (review-workspace.tsx:426-429), while the button "All N changed views…" opens a confirmation dialog first (1042-1059, 1242-1296).

title: Arrow keys are taken from focusable scroll regions and from the page
summary: With a 200% image viewport focused, ArrowDown changed the item and scrollTop stayed 0; ArrowRight changed the variant; only PageDown/Space scroll. The viewport is a focusable `overflow-auto` div (screenshot-viewer.tsx:132-137).

title: Zoomed panes pan independently
summary: Each ImagePane keeps its own scroll position (screenshot-viewer.tsx:34-48); after scrolling Baseline to [200,150] Current stayed at [0,0], and each pane has its own four pan buttons.

title: Shortcut help is hard to find, hints are always on, and the toggle is not remembered
summary: Help opens only from a 26px footer icon that is below the fold at all 5 viewports (tab stop 23 of 24); `?` does nothing; hints stay when shortcuts are off; `useState(true)` resets on reload; one `aria-keyshortcuts`; vendored Kbd unused.

title: Focus ring clipped on the main navigation, the review search, and the item rows
summary: The horizontal Nav is its own scroll container (`overflow-x-auto`, nav.ariakit.react.tsx:73) with no padding, so 3 of 4 ring sides are cut; `pt-0!` and `.review-item-scroll overflow-auto` cut the search and row rings.

title: The history search field has no focus ring
summary: routes/index.tsx:661 uses `outline-none focus-visible:underline`; the only focus cue is a 1px underline under the placeholder (4.00:1 in light), unlike the review search which rings its frame.

title: Selected variant is weak in dark, invisible in light, and equal to the others in forced colors
summary: Selected pill fill is 1.26:1 in dark and 1.02:1 in light where unselected pills have the visible outline; in forced colors selected and unselected have identical computed styles.

title: Variant pills do not show the review status
summary: variant-summary.tsx renders no verdict; status exists only in `aria-label` and `title` (review-workspace.tsx:747, 776), so approved, rejected, error and unchanged pills look the same.

title: The variant strip hides most variants and costs one tab stop per variant
summary: With 7 variants: 1 visible at 390, 2 at 768/1024, 3 at 1440, 5 at 1920; 959px hidden at 1440 with no scrollbar or fade; 7 tab stops; number keys cover 1-6 only; each pill repeats shared label parts.

title: `$layer="primary"` is not a layer color: primary buttons render gray, and three sign-in buttons differ
summary: The vendored layer knows canvas/brand/secondary/success/warning/danger only; `primary` becomes an invalid `--layer-color`, so 6 call sites render #000 on #eee in both schemes; the run guest button is flat with no fill.

title: Controls use 40% to 66% of the viewport above the image; sticky bars leave 71px at 400% zoom
summary: Image top is at 431px of 900 (1440), 425 of 768 (1024), 561 of 844 (390); the page always scrolls and the footer is below the fold; at 320x256 the sticky bars total 185px (72%).

title: The mobile review flow is a stacked desktop page
summary: At 390x844 the page is 1685px tall with two stacked 521px panes, a 91px two-row action bar, keyboard hints on touch, a clipped view-mode strip, and an item dialog that stays open after select.

title: Every page has the same title; client navigation drops focus; header links reload the document
summary: Only `__root.tsx:10` sets a title ("Visonaut"); after client navigation focus is on body; header links and the workspace "Queue" link are plain anchors that each cause a full document load; no skip link.

title: The end of a review has no visible state
summary: "Review complete. No variants need review." goes only to the visually hidden live region (use-review-session.ts:366-368); the screen keeps the last variant with Approve enabled.

title: A quarter of the review text is below 12px, and fixed pixel sizes ignore the user font size
summary: 26 of 100 text runs in the review page are 10-11px; 18 `text-[10px|11px|13px]` uses (all buttons and nav) do not scale with the default font size, so the hierarchy inverts at 32px.

title: Contrast below 4.5:1 for placeholders and for `opacity-50` text in the light scheme
summary: Review search placeholder is 2.19:1 (dark) and 1.84:1 (light); `opacity-50` text at 10-12px is 3.96:1 in light; history placeholder 4.00:1. `ak-ink-60` text passes (5.71:1 / 7.26:1).

title: Pointer targets are 19px to 35px
summary: At 390 with touch: brand link 19x23, history select 104x19, view modes 25px, Undo 26px, header links 32px, Approve 34.5px; 31 targets, 2 below 24px, none reaches 44px.

title: The color scheme follows the system only, and the image stage has no backdrop control
summary: The only scheme switch is `@variant dark` on `--color-canvas` (ui.css:75-82); no toggle or stored preference; light captures blend into the light stage and dark captures into the dark stage.

title: Semantics: unnamed focus targets, one heading on the review page, heading jumps, `title` as the only tooltip
summary: Three focusable `div`s have `aria-label` and no role; the review page has one heading (item name); H1 to H3 jumps in service and popover; 13 `title` tooltips; one unnamed group; `<time>` without `dateTime`.

title: Three vocabularies for the same controls, and the review guide does not match the UI
summary: Buttons say Compare/Difference/Current/Baseline, accessible names say Reference/New image/Pixel diff, help and guide say Side by side/Original only; view/variant/screenshot/item mix; guide lacks `[` and names "All runs".

title: Shortcuts read `event.key`, so `[` and letters fail on some keyboard layouts
summary: The handler returns when Alt is down and compares `event.key` (review-workspace.tsx:398-399): `[` typed with AltGr and a Cyrillic key on KeyA were ignored in synthetic tests.

title: Reduced motion is respected for large motion; small transitions remain
summary: Under reduce the sidebar settles in one frame (285ms otherwise) and popovers have no transition; 41 press-scale and 5 glider transitions (100ms) remain; popover open is 500ms with overshoot when motion is allowed.

title: Dashboard status color and icon do not follow the status
summary: `reviewing` gets the label "Needs review" but no warning color (routes/index.tsx:132, 142-151); every In progress and Needs attention row uses a clock icon; "1 view await approval" grammar.

title: Keyboard shortcuts stop after a mouse click on a variant chip
summary: `.review-variants` is in the shortcut exclusion selector (review-workspace.tsx:95), so after a chip click A, X, S, D, F, G, 1-6, Up and Down are ignored (measured: A saved 0 commands; same on the real route).

title: The selected variant chip scrolls out of view and nothing else names the selected variant
summary: The chip strip is 2079 px wide in a 1120 px box and never scrolls on shortcut or auto-advance selection (scrollLeft stays 0), so after 3 approvals no chip looks selected; decision: which switcher replaces the strip.

title: Approve & next moves 20 px after the first decision and a repeat click misses
summary: The save-state row grows the sticky bar from 61 to 81 px (97 px on error); a second click at the same pointer position saved 0 commands at 1440x900, 1280x720 and 390x844.

title: Variant chips do not show the verdict
summary: variant-summary.tsx never reads verdict or kind, so approved, rejected, error and pending chips look the same; only the selected variant has a badge.

title: 408 px of chrome sits above the first screenshot pixel
summary: Seven stacked rows take 45.3% of 1440x900, 56.7% of 1280x720 and 61.4% of 390x844 before the image, plus a 61 px decision bar; at 1280x720 Fit does not fit (229 of 317 px visible).

title: A disabled Approve & next keeps its brand fill and looks enabled
summary: Disabled and enabled states have the same background oklch(0.515 0.155 248.5); only label alpha changes to 0.73 (vendored control.ts disabled classes use bg-none, which clears the image only).

title: The viewer jumps 41 px down and back up each time images load
summary: The loading strip is a block row above the panes (review-workspace.tsx:940-949): viewer top 342, then 383 while loading, then 342.

title: Key presses during image load are dropped without feedback and nothing is preloaded
summary: `if (!ready) return` discards A, A, X while the next images load (calls stayed 1, announcement empty); no preload or prefetch exists in the review code.

title: Warning and alert banners have no visual treatment
summary: Four banners use `ak-layer-warning` without the `ak-layer` base (review-workspace.tsx:690-706); measured background is rgba(0,0,0,0) with no border or radius.

title: Save errors, conflicts and success use the same small gray text
summary: Not saved, Conflict and Saved all render as 12 px ak-ink-60 text in the bar corner, and the Retry and Refresh buttons have no border or fill.

title: A click or a key in the search field opens the status menu, which covers the results
summary: The search input is the Combobox of the status filter: its 165 px popover opens on click and on typing and covers 3 result rows; the tests press Escape after each fill.

title: Approve & next ignores the active search and filter
summary: nextPending runs on the full model (use-review-session.ts:313) while arrows use the filtered order; with search 'Open menu' the page jumped to 'Success dialog', which is not in the list.

title: Status and counts are shown in up to 11 places
summary: 145 words in 95 text nodes above the fold and 6 occurrences of 'need(s) review'; also plural errors '1 changed pixels' and 'All 1 changed views...'.

title: The progress bar is full green on a rejected run and starts almost full on large runs
summary: The native progress counts any verdict and every unchanged capture as done (review-workspace.tsx:317-326, 599-604) and renders green in both schemes.

title: There is no visible review-complete state
summary: 'Review complete. No variants need review.' goes only to the sr-only live region; sighted users see '0 of 11 need review' and 10 px 'Check passed'.

title: The decision bar renders with nothing to decide and floats mid-page
summary: Empty runs, closed summaries and read-only runs still show Undo, 'All 0 changed views...', Reject and a bright Approve; with short content the sticky bar sits at y = 333 to 433.

title: The whole-item command is inconsistent between trigger, modal, keyboard and labels
summary: A chevron button opens a modal; the mouse path needs 2 clicks and a confirmation while Shift+A saves at once; three names for one command; 'All 1 changed views...'.

title: The recompare UI is dead in production
summary: api/review.ts:592 always sends recompareAllowed false and the endpoint always throws, but the footer button, reason text, banner, hook state and tests remain (about 80 lines).

title: Keyboard help and the shortcut toggle are always below the fold
summary: The static footer needs a page scroll at every tested viewport (994 vs 900, 893 vs 720); the toggle is not saved and key hints stay visible when shortcuts are off.

title: Three vocabularies in the UI and a fourth in the review guide
summary: variant, view and capture; baseline, reference and original; current, new image and candidate; approved and accepted; the guide names the view buttons differently and says 'All runs' for 'Queue'.

title: In the light scheme the selected chip and list row are almost invisible
summary: Selection uses `$lighten: 2`, which has no room on white; the selected chip is the only chip without an outline.

title: Seven font sizes, 16 text elements at 10 px, two unstyled 16 px outliers
summary: Sizes 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 28 px; 'Accepted (N)' and the footer reason fall back to 16 px; 130 className attributes, 5 dimming values and 17 important overrides in the lane files.

title: The item row spends its space on a 26 px thumbnail and hides useful state
summary: Thumbnail renders at 26x26 in a 44 px row; a rejected variant hides the pending count; no New badge; accepted rows say '0 of N need review'; the header count ignores the filter.

title: Each variant chip is 265 to 307 px wide because it repeats the same facts
summary: The label repeats framework, browser and scheme as icons, text and the variant key, plus unlabeled icons for default contrast and forced colors; 12 variants need about 3,500 px.

title: The Details panel repeats the header, prints raw IDs and has unstyled links
summary: Three first lines repeat on-page facts, IDs are not copyable, history links look like text, and the panel takes 256 px of image width.

title: Phone layout: 518 px of controls before the image and small targets
summary: At 390x844: 11 control rows, 213 px of image, a 91 px bar (165 px on error), targets down to 19x23 px, stacked panes, and key hints on touch.

title: Hand-built UI stands where Ariakit UI primitives exist
summary: Native progress, 4 raw dialogs, 9 title tooltips, raw banners and dl lists; Kbd, Tabs and TextFrame are vendored but unused; upstream dialog, tooltip, progress, input and combobox are not vendored (contract D10 freezes the set).

title: Queue and history links are plain anchors that reload the document
summary: review-workspace.tsx:580 and :474-487 use `<a href>`; a click on Queue caused 1 document load; three links to '/' sit in the top 96 px.

title: 30 Tab stops come before Approve & next
summary: Each of the 7 chips, 4 view buttons and 3 zoom buttons is a separate Tab stop; composite groups would give about 19 stops.

title: review-workspace.tsx is one 1,100-line component
summary: ReviewSession (lines 195-1299) holds 12 useState, 5 effects, a 13-branch key handler, 4 dialogs and all layout; the disabled rule is written 5 times.

title: The sidebar preference needs an inline head script on every route
summary: The run route is `ssr: false`, so the useState initializer could read localStorage directly; no CSS reads the data attribute that the head script sets.

title: Row click selects the first pending variant but arrow keys select the remembered one
summary: In route mode the row Link uses variantKeyForItem (first pending), while selectItem prefers the remembered variant; the fixture has no route, so tests do not see it. Note of revision r9: the two rules are the rule that the maintainer selected (D04, U03, pull request #104). The review record of pull request #104 declined a row link that uses the remembered variant.

title: Status polling runs every 2 seconds with no backoff
summary: use-review-session.ts:185-258 polls /state every 2 s while a run is incomplete or comparing: 1,800 requests per hour per open tab (counted from code).

title: Small visual defects in the sidebar
summary: Row focus ring is cut at the sides, the filter box touches the header divider (pt-0!), and Accepted rows have a different indent, hover fill and two size caps.

title: The pull request page is a client-side redirect hop in front of every review
summary: GitHub check Details -> SSR loading shell -> /api/pulls (full access check) -> run chunk -> /api/runs/:id (access check again); +487 ms against the direct run URL with 300 ms injected per API call.

title: The service status page waits for the run list, and it disappears when the run list fails
summary: /?view=service mounts the alerts only after /api/runs succeeds (sequential requests); a failing /api/runs shows only a queue error and never asks for alerts.

title: Header links to "Service status" reload the document and fetch everything again
summary: Header NavLink is a plain anchor: a click from the queue causes document + /api/runs + /api/operations although the bell already holds the alerts.

title: The alert poll never pauses, misses the permission cache on idle tabs, and scans the whole event table
summary: 60 s poll continues in hidden tabs (measured), each idle poll re-checks GitHub permission (code), 3 unbatched D1 reads plus a duplicate project read, and SCAN operations_events with no index and no row deletion (query plan).

title: One failed background poll ends the waiting state, and waiting has no upper bound
summary: A single 503 during the 15 s poll replaces "Waiting for screenshots" with "Review unavailable" and stops polling; a pending check is polled 40 times per 10 minutes with no backoff or limit.

title: The page is bound to one check attempt and cannot find the current review of the pull request
summary: Lookup is by check external ID only; old or rerun links show the old attempt forever, and /pulls/N without check returns 404 with no link.

title: Several states are dead ends or give no feedback
summary: Not-found says "open GitHub" with no GitHub link, failed state offers a useless "Check again", "Check again" changes nothing visible, and a failed sign-in shows "Review unavailable".

title: Preview shows false messages on both surfaces
summary: In preview the pull page shows "Repository access required / Use another account" and the service page shows "Last checked Dec 31, 1969" (checkedAt: 0).

title: $layer="primary" is not a layer color, so primary buttons are neutral gray
summary: The vendored Layer accepts canvas/brand/secondary/success/warning/danger; "primary" becomes an invalid CSS color, so 6 primary CTAs render light gray (1.16:1 against the card in light mode).

title: ak-ink-danger, ak-ink-warning, and ak-ink-success do not exist, so error text has no color
summary: ak-ink-* takes only a number; the built CSS has no such rules, so alert error text and the bell "!" mark compute to the normal text color.

title: The service page column moves with its content
summary: max-w-4xl mx-auto on a Shell grid item shrinks the panel to its content: h1 left edge is 398 px with no alerts and 272 px with seven; the Shell bands are not used.

title: The alert text catalogue does not match the alerts that the service emits
summary: 10 emitted kinds fall to one generic card, backup and backup-retention branches have no emitter, one text covers three capacity codes, and tests and the guide still use the retired backup kind.

title: A malformed capacity snapshot hides every alert
summary: The server passes the capacity cursor through unvalidated and the client throws on any bad field, discarding the events with it.

title: Alert cards do not say what is affected, since when, or how bad it is
summary: Cards are title + paragraph + closed details with no severity, time, subject, count, or link; 7 alerts = 1528 px and 258 words, and the popover shows 2 of 7 cards (1 of 7 on mobile).

title: Both surfaces say the same thing several times
summary: The empty service page has 9 text blocks and 64 words, states "no alerts" twice, and always shows three disclaimers; the pull card repeats the pull request number in eyebrow and heading.

title: One concept has five names and two entry points in the same header
summary: Service status, Service attention, Operations, operation alerts, and service alert name the same list; the bell and the nav link both open it and do not link to each other.

title: The pull request page has no pull request context and no stage information
summary: /api/pulls returns only repository, number, runId, and state; the page shows no title, commit, attempt, stage, elapsed time, or workflow link, and "pending" covers several different situations.

title: Three different sign-in and access-denied designs, and three different headers
summary: Dashboard, run, and pull pages each have their own sign-in and denied copy, buttons, and header contents; the account menu never shows the signed-in login.

title: Layout and style defects on the pull request page
summary: Back link is a 592 px centered button above left-aligned content, the pending status frame is invisible and indents text 48 px, failure uses saturated warning yellow, and same-tab actions carry an external-link arrow.

title: The surfaces bypass primitives that the vendored copy already has
summary: Native details instead of Disclosure, a custom scroll div instead of PopoverScroll, max-w/mx-auto instead of Shell bands, Text used only with raw classes, test-hook class names with no CSS; upstream Progress/List/Heading are not vendored.

title: Accessibility gaps
summary: Heading order h1 -> h3, a second h1 from popover headings, the same document title "Visonaut" on every route, repeated live announcements on remount, and focus lost on state changes; no text contrast failure found.

title: "Open the operations and recovery guide" does not lead to recovery steps for the alert
summary: One fixed link to apps/web/src/operations/README.md, which has no section for check reconciliation, check delivery, or promotion retry that the alert texts refer to.

title: One component holds polling, announcements, copy, and two layouts, and the page layout has no test
summary: operations-attention/index.tsx (518 lines) mixes parsing, catalogue, polling, and 8 layout branches; no browser test covers /?view=service, and the fixture renders without the Shell.

title: Timestamps and sizes are hard to read
summary: Only absolute date-times (two clocks on one screen) and capacity as "1612.4 MiB used; 435.6 MiB before new runs pause" with no relative time, duration, or meter.

title: A review that waits for a maintainer is a red failure, and three different states share one title
summary: run-status.ts:98-105 maps needs-review, rejected, and failed to failure, and checks.ts:51-54 gives all three the title "Visual review has not passed"; the three states need three different actions.

title: "Visual review is running" also means "waits for a person" and "needs a new capture"
summary: Merge queue needs-review and needs-recompare fall into the pending branch (run-status.ts:103-105) and show the in_progress title of the upload and comparison stages, although nothing runs and server recompare is disabled (review.ts:986).

title: The check output has no counts and no item names. The service computes the counts and drops them
summary: One sentence serves all run states (checks.ts:44); pending and rejected counts are read at run-status.ts:56-60 and :94 but only the conclusion is stored; each decision already triggers a GET and PATCH with the same text; public output conflicts with review-guide.md:3 unless decided.

title: The check tells each reader to sign in. A pull request author who does so reaches a dead end
summary: The summary and contributing.md:578 send the author to the review; after the OAuth grant the run page shows "This run could not be opened" with only Retry and no account menu, and a user, account, session, and audit row stay in D1.

title: The page behind the Details link contradicts the check in three states

summary: wrangler.jsonc has no placement; production from GRU shows 154 ms for a 1-query path vs 23-34 ms for /health, so 15 sequential round trips in GET /api/runs/:id is an estimated 1.9-2.5 s of D1 wait. Option: Smart Placement. D1 region not verified.

title: The run model reads the same rows again and awaits 15 round trips in sequence
summary: GET /api/runs/:id makes 21 D1 round trips (project read 3 times, run 2-3 times, comparison 2 times; readRunStatus awaits 6 reads one by one; two R2 inventory reads are sequential). One batch keyed by run ID can cut the depth from 15 to about 4.

title: Each model read downloads, hashes, and validates two complete inventories from R2
summary: reviewModel reads both immutable inventory objects on every call (9.4 MB and 166 ms Node CPU at 3,582 captures), rehashes, re-canonicalizes, validates each capture, and round-trips each capture through JSON strings; this repeats on every receipt and Undo.

title: The first response contains each unchanged capture, although the page needs only the changed ones first
summary: The model has about 600 bytes per capture for all captures (633 KB raw at 1,058, 2.15 MB at 3,582) while unchanged items sit in a closed Accepted group; an attention-first response needs D1 only and no R2. Contract line 26 mentions full-inventory reads.

title: Each saved decision and each Undo builds and returns the complete model again
summary: The receipt endpoint (review.ts:812-832) and Undo (commandResult) rebuild the full model (23 and 30 D1 round trips measured) although the stored receipt is sufficient and applySavedReview already handles a receipt without a model.

title: Save confirmation has a fixed 500 ms wait, a late session request, and a permission cache that write requests clear
summary: client.ts sleeps 500 ms before the first receipt poll, creates the review session on the first Approve, and authorization.ts deletes but does not re-store the permission after live write checks (48 GitHub permission calls for 12 cycles).

title: Each first view of an image goes through the Worker, D1, and R2 with no edge cache
summary: /images/:id does 1 D1 query plus 1 R2 read per request and never uses the Cache API, so `immutable` helps only one browser; the D1 lookup alone is 154 ms TTFB in production and Approve stays disabled until both images decode.

title: The page does not preload the next images
summary: No preload exists for the next pending variant, adjacent variants, or the diff mask; nextPending already knows the target, so each Approve or arrow key waits for fresh image requests.

title: The model request can start only after all JavaScript is loaded and hydrated
summary: `ssr: false` plus a client loader makes HTML -> 230 KB brotli of assets -> hydration -> API -> render -> images strictly serial (API starts at 1,875 ms on the slow profile); an inline script in the shell can start the fetch in parallel.

title: The pull-request page makes a second authenticated round trip before the run starts to load
summary: /pulls/:n hydrates, calls /api/pulls (8 D1 round trips, 6 of them the repeated preamble), navigates, lazy-loads 4 run chunks, then calls /api/runs; a server redirect or a combined response removes one hop (estimated 1.0-1.3 s).

title: Hashed assets are revalidated on each load, and main navigation reloads the document
summary: Assets are served with `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` (no public/_headers), so 10 conditional requests run per document load and the favicon revalidates per variant change; header links are plain anchors and the router has no defaultPreload.

title: The waits show text only, the layout moves, and a signed-out visitor waits for a 401
summary: The pending shell is one grey line with no workspace frame; three loading texts show at once; the viewer shifts 41 px on each image load; a visitor without a session cookie waits 515-569 ms for a 401 before the sign-in card.

title: The sidebar thumbnail has no source in current runs
summary: `thumbnailImageId` is written only by the retired compare Worker; local-v1 results never set it, so every sidebar row of a new run shows a dash while test fixtures show thumbnails.

title: A cold isolate makes three GitHub calls in sequence before any data is read
summary: Installation token, login hint, and permission caches live only in isolate memory, so the first private request after a cold start does token mint, GET /user/:id, and the permission read one after the other; cold frequency and GitHub latency not measured.

title: The CLI stops on answers that the server marks as temporary
summary: Server uses 503 + Retry-After: 1 for waiting states (55 throw sites, 10 codes); the CLI retries only 2 codes on GET/PUT/reuse, so no OIDC or service request of an unchanged Submit (27 of 36 requests) has a retry and network errors are never retried.

title: The CLI hides the cause of most failures
summary: Five catch blocks replace specific errors with general sentences; server error.code and error.reference are dropped, a 503 during begin returns exit 4, a wrong job-name template returns 'The verified capture submission failed.', and no message names the item or limit.

title: Image and capture limits differ in six places, and the smallest limit applies last
summary: Adapter accepts 20 MiB and 32 MP, trusted Submit accepts 2 MiB, 2.1 MP, 8192 px; the largest documented Ariakit capture (1248x1650) is at 98.1% of the pixel limit and an oversize capture fails only in Submit with 'Capture the image again'.

title: Submit decodes each candidate PNG two times, also when the bytes equal the reference
summary: validateLocalImages and compareLocally both fully decode every capture; in an unchanged run 90-100% of compareLocally time is spent before the digest equality check (3.9-5.1 ms per real 640x360 image, 42-55 ms per synthetic large image).

title: Service.status() makes 5 to 6 sequential round trips and reads rows that the caller already has
summary: readRunStatus runs run, comparison, a legacy dead-task join, counts, project, and promotion as separate awaits; review page load and each poll (7-8 sequential round trips) repeat reads of run, comparison, and project; one database.batch would make it 1 round trip.

title: The comparison identities accept one value, and stored manifests are validated again on each read
summary: validateLocalComparison accepts only 'playwright-pixelmatch-1.63.0' and 'pngjs-7.0.0', stored inventories pass through parseManifest on every read, and no test or Renovate rule binds the constants to the installed pngjs/pixelmatch versions.

title: A run that expired before completion gets the label "superseded"
summary: reviewStatus checks active before state, so a run closed by expireIncompleteWorkflowRun (active=0, state='failed') returns 'superseded'; two apps/web callers correct this by hand and the dashboard shows 'Replaced by a newer run'.

title: The published CLI contains removed commands, and most transport tests use them
summary: About 75 engine lines for upload, submit --run, submit JSON output, and transfer-key are unreachable from runCli and rejected by the server, still ship in visonaut@0.5.4, and 29 test invocations drive the transport code through the removed upload command.

title: @visonaut/service keeps queue publication code and legacy compare-task statements that production does not use
summary: reconcileWork (158 lines) has no production caller, reportComparisonPublication is called with constant empty lists, and reserveRun, retireRun, and status() still run statements for compare tasks that no source file creates.

title: The write path for runs without an inventory remains, and most test fixtures use it
summary: The only production commitShard caller always passes an inventory, but about 270 service lines plus rendering-profile-conversion.ts serve the old form, and the shared fixtures (test-fixtures.ts, 12 of 16 commitShard calls in service.test.ts) build runs in that old form.

title: The protocol README and about 230 lines of validators describe a flow that the server does not use
summary: parseTrustedPlan, validateShardDeclaration, validateShardAgainstPlan, validateCollection, PROTOCOL_MAJOR, and 10 HTTP types have no importer outside protocol tests; the README shows them as server usage, lists 5 of 11 endpoints, and names the wrong finalize response.

title: Paths, schema versions, and error shapes of the wire contract have more than one source
summary: schemaVersion is 1 for /v1/plan and "1.0" elsewhere, two version regexes disagree, 2 of 8 TRANSPORT entries are unused while the CLI hand-builds 5 paths, three shard-key grammars exist, all ProtocolError codes become invalid_manifest, and a missing run returns 409.

title: The published visonaut bundle contains pngjs and pixelmatch without their license notices
summary: tsup bundles pngjs (MIT) and pixelmatch (ISC) into dist; the published 0.5.4 chunk (202,387 bytes) has zero license or copyright strings, LICENSE names only Ariakit, and the CI package check would reject an added notice file.

title: Three READMEs state old versions or old behavior
summary: The CLI README (also in the published 0.5.4 tarball) says 0.5.3, the root README says 0.5.3 and adapter 0.4.0 while the contract says 0.5.4 and 0.5.0, two sentences still promise legacy uploads, and no document says how to get VISONAUT_TOKEN for status.

title: Argument errors and progress output of the CLI are hard to use
summary: Unknown or removed flags and 'submit --help' answer 'Each required shard must be a unique stable key.', there is no --version, Submit prints no comparison summary or review URL and is silent for steps 2-9, and environment variables are validated after the App check starts.

title: GitHub API calls in the CLI have no retry, three time-out rules, and two pagination loops
summary: github-artifacts uses a 30 s time-out, signed-context uses none, the artifact body has 120 s for up to 1 GiB; HTTP failures on download report a malformed archive, pagination is implemented twice with different stop rules, and historical job lists are fetched again for each shard.

title: Reference downloads are sequential, and three server write loops use small pages
summary: compareLocally downloads one reference per changed capture with no concurrency, a capability renewal re-reads all 18 reference pages, and commitShard spends 36 assertion-only round trips for 3,582 captures because the page size is 100.

title: Conventions differ between the packages, and the protocol tests are not type-checked
summary: protocol tsconfig includes only src, hiding one TS2532 error in test/protocol.test.ts:247; five tsconfig forms, .js versus .ts import suffixes, undeclared devDependencies in service, a SHA-256 hex encoder written 8 times, readOne/readRows 7 times, and six type names defined twice.

title: The adapter waits a fixed 100 ms and decodes two PNGs for each capture, and the reporter loads modules that it does not use
summary: Each visual() call sleeps at least 100 ms and decodes both screenshots (30-47 ms measured versus 0.05 ms to compare encoded bytes), the published reporter.js imports @playwright/test and pngjs for two constants, and the font list that feeds fontsDigest is sorted with ICU collation.

title: Each API request runs a full database schema check inside better-auth
summary: createAuth builds a new better-auth 1.7.5 instance per request; each one sends 1 sqlite_master query + 1 batch of 75 pragma_table_info statements before any auth call. Guest /api/me 344-351 ms and /api/runs 366-413 ms vs 28 ms without auth. advanced.database.validateSchema:false gives 0 statements locally.

title: One D1 round trip costs about 90 ms from GRU, and a signed-in API request makes 6 to 9 in series
summary: Measured: 1 extra point query adds 85-135 ms (/api/runs/<id> 453-517 ms vs /api/runs 366-384 ms). Counted from code, not measured: /api/runs 6 and /api/operations 9 serial D1 round trips when signed in. No placement setting; operationsStatus reads the project a second time.

title: The first data request starts only after all JavaScript has loaded and run
summary: SSR always sends 'Checking access'; index.tsx fetches in useEffect and the run route has ssr:false. Production guest: loading line on screen 406 ms cold, 454 ms warm, 940 ms with 4x CPU + slow 4G, 535 ms on the run page; the API wait is 92% of it.

title: /api/operations starts only after /api/runs ends, and repeats the auth work
summary: OperationsAttention mounts only when the run list is ready (index.tsx:254-256), then sends a second request with 9 D1 round trips and repeats it each 60 s. Needs a session to measure.

title: Hashed assets are served with max-age=0, must-revalidate
summary: No _headers file. A warm load of the production home page sent 10 conditional requests, all 304, 46-98 ms wait each; scripts were usable only after them.

title: A cold Worker adds about 300 to 450 ms to the document
summary: Document wait 354-511 ms with cfEdge 199-267 ms on cold hits vs 56-131 ms with cfEdge 9-21 ms warm (preview cold on 3 of 3 new connections, production on 1 of 3). Server build is 4.1 MB of unminified JS (888 KB gzip); the link to startup time is an assumption.

title: One 465 KB stylesheet blocks first paint, and the HTML is mostly class names
summary: index-CXm4JU5N.css is 46,757 bytes on the wire and 464,666 decoded for all routes; home JS is 205 KB wire / 602 KB decoded in 8 files (3 icon chunks under 500 bytes); 72% of the 29 KB document is class attributes. FCP 228 ms fast link, 2392 ms with slow 4G + 4x CPU.

title: Cloudflare Web Analytics is injected into every page and the repository does not mention it
summary: Both hosts add static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js (nonce copied past the CSP) and one POST /cdn-cgi/rum per page view; no reference in the repository. It also means real-user load data already exists in the Cloudflare dashboard.

title: The preview deployment does not match main
summary: Preview serves markup and asset names from before PR #252 (matches e277a91/242d371, not f83fef6); production matches the local HEAD build. preview-web is a manual dispatch and /health exposes no commit.

title: Unknown URLs give a bare 'Not Found' page
summary:
A path with no route (also a missing /assets file) returns 404 HTML with only

Not Found

; no notFoundComponent is set in router.tsx or __root.tsx.

title: No recovery when a lazy chunk is missing after a deploy
summary: Not reproduced. Missing assets return 404 HTML, there is no vite:preloadError handler, the run route is a separate chunk, and production deploys on each push to main.

title: Error bodies and headers differ between routes
summary: /api/runs 401 has schemaVersion and no Retry-After; /api/me 401 has no schemaVersion, sends Retry-After: 1, and is logged as an operation failure; /health and /images 404 lack the security header set.

title: API responses have no application Server-Timing
summary: All 29 API and health responses sampled with curl lack server-timing; only documents carry Cloudflare's cfEdge/cfWorker. Auth, GitHub, and D1 time cannot be attributed from the browser.

title: Each return to the queue loads the run list again and shows the loading line again
summary: Index starts in 'loading' and fetches on every mount with no cache (index.tsx:161,176-210); the run route uses gcTime: 0. From code only; needs a session to measure.

title: Better Auth reads the whole database schema on every request
summary: A new Better Auth instance per request runs schema validation each time: 2 extra serial D1 round trips (76 statements, about 85 KB) and about 330 ms from GRU on every private request, guest request, and CI upload; `advanced.database.validateSchema: false` removes it (measured 5 to 3 round trips in requireMaintainer).

title: The server sends the loading text, and the data request starts only after hydration
summary: The `/` route has no loader, so the server HTML always contains "Checking access and loading runs…" and `/api/runs` starts only after 602 KB of JS loads and hydrates (166-367 ms guest, 240-595 ms signed in); a server loader or streamed loader removes the JS gate and one browser round trip without changing the access check.

title: Each D1 round trip costs about 105-125 ms from the São Paulo edge, and the Worker has no placement setting
summary: Production probes at GRU show 32 ms with no D1, 157 ms with one D1 round trip, and +106 ms per further round trip; private reads make 6-9 serial round trips and wrangler.jsonc has no `placement`, so smart or targeted placement near D1 is the main latency lever (database region not verified).

title: The access check and the operations read send their D1 statements one at a time
summary: Session and user are two statements because Better Auth joins are off, the account lookup is a third, `/api/operations` checks the project twice and runs 3 independent statements serially; `joins: true` plus one batch brings `/api/runs` from 6 to 3 and `/api/operations` from 9 to 3 round trips (with LOAD-01).

title: Each header navigation click reloads the whole document
summary: `AppHeader` uses plain `href` anchors, so Review queue, Run history, and Service status each cause a full document load, 9 asset revalidations, hydration, and a new access check, while the in-page router `Link` to the same view causes zero requests.

title: The dashboard data lives only in component state
summary: Browser Back from a run and the `Refresh runs` button both reset the page to the loading text; during a refresh the queue, the alert bell, and the account menu are removed and the bell refetches when it returns.

title: The service view and the alert bell wait for /api/runs before they request /api/operations
summary: `OperationsAttention` mounts only after `/api/runs` succeeds, so the service view runs two full access checks in sequence (15 serial D1 round trips; alerts visible at about 2.7 s signed in) although it needs only `preview` and `repository` from the first read.
