title: The alert poll period equals the permission cache lifetime, so each poll calls GitHub
summary: The bell polls 60 s after each response and the read permission cache lasts 60 s from the start of the check, so every poll misses the cache: 1 GitHub call, 9 D1 round trips, and 83 statements per minute per open tab, also when the tab is hidden.

title: The permission, token, and login caches live in one isolate only
summary: The first signed-in read in each new isolate makes 3 serial GitHub calls (token, user by ID, permission); a D1-stored grant with `checked_at`, read in the same batch as the account lookup, keeps the 60 s and 10 s limits and removes the calls across isolates.

title: A cold Worker adds 0.6-1.3 s to the first request
summary: 2 of 8 new production connections needed 702 ms and 1,402 ms for the first `/health` (others 83-232 ms); the Worker is 33 modules, 4.1 MB raw, with an unminified 2.1 MB entry; the startup time itself is not known.

title: Content-hashed assets are revalidated on every document load
summary: Production serves `/assets/*` with `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so each document load sends 9 conditional requests before hydration; a `public/_headers` rule with `immutable` removes them.

title: Opening a run from the queue shows no change for 1 second, and nothing is preloaded
summary: The router default `pendingMs` of 1,000 ms keeps the queue on screen with no feedback for 1 s after `Review changes`, then shows a text-only pending page; no link sets `preload`, so the run chunk and model start only after the click.

title: Pull request titles are erased before the dashboard reads them
summary: `processWebhook` sets `payload_json = '{}'` after each delivery, but the dashboard and run page read the PR title from that payload, so titles disappear after processing; reproduced locally and visible in production (`#7746 · Pull request`).

title: /api/me and /api/session are not used by the app, and their error shape differs
summary: Two identity endpoints exist with duplicate auth wiring, the UI calls neither and the user menu shows no login; `/api/me` errors have `Retry-After: 1` and no `schemaVersion`, unlike `/api/runs`; a doc line still says routes call `/api/me` first.

title: The dashboard leaves 401 and 403 response bodies unread
summary: On 401 or 403 the client returns without reading or cancelling the body, so Chrome never finishes the request and the guest page never reaches network idle (Playwright `networkidle` timed out on production).

title: A failed GitHub read marks a check "ambiguous" forever
summary: deliverStatus sets request_started before the sender runs and treats every sender error as ambiguous (packages/service/src/work.ts:491-548); a failed GET before the PATCH locks the check until a manual D1 repair, and no repair procedure or tool exists.

title: An ambiguous check with a newer status starts an endless status loop, and each cron tick adds one more loop
summary: operations/checks.ts:347-349 counts an "attention" outcome as more work, so runtime.ts:446-454 re-sends status every second and every recovery pass starts another chain (queue depth 1..6 over six ticks, 33 D1 round trips per loop pass).

title: Two statements in each status pass read (accepted runs x snapshots) rows
summary: statusRunEligibleSql (packages/service/src/review-status.ts:25-27) scans visonaut_snapshots for each accepted run: 999,999 full-scan steps at 1,000 runs; a rewritten predicate needs 999.

title: The review-links step pages through every pull request on every cron tick
summary: publishReviewLinks has no state or time filter and reports hasMore for full pages of rows it skips; one tick causes floor(P/25) extra status passes (41 passes, 1,363 round trips at 1,000 pull requests).

title: Webhook delivery recovery runs 3 D1 statements for each listed delivery, including successful ones
summary: operations/github-deliveries.ts:229-246 does a SELECT and two UPDATEs per delivery: 303 of the 383 round trips of an idle pass; the cursor walk also delays detection of new failed deliveries.

title: Two alerts are resolved by an operation that did not fix them
summary: The runtime reconciler kind "checks" collides with the step "checks" (runtime.ts:371, operations/index.ts:49,80), and the runtime scheduler alert is resolved by any successful pass of any kind (runtime.ts:455).

title: Several alerts never clear, and one alert fires for normal retries
summary: check-creation and promotion alerts of a closed run stayed listed after ten recovery passes; redelivery-exhausted and expired-incomplete have no resolver once their subject is gone; staged reconciliation records an alert for expected not-ready retries.

title: A failed pass leaves no cause in the logs, and log shapes differ
summary: catch blocks in server.ts:164-167, operations/index.ts:81-88 and runtime.ts drop the error; the pass log has no kind, step, or subject; event names and duration fields use mixed conventions.

title: A stopped scheduler, a dead-lettered message, or a killed pass raises no signal
summary: The Service view shows the API read time as "Last checked", there is no heartbeat or notification, the dead-letter queue has no consumer (4-day retention), and a platform-killed invocation skips the alert and the 60-second retry delay.

title: Failure isolation is not the same for all parts of a pass
summary: The ten steps are isolated, but the pre-steps (operations/index.ts:32-46), expireExports (index.ts:96-110) and the prepareStatusIntent loop are not; one error aborts the pass, drops continuations, and causes full-pass retries.

title: One queue with one consumer puts check updates and ingest behind maintenance, and the wait is not measured
summary: max_concurrency 1 serializes status and ingest behind long recovery work; repository evidence records 21 to 33 s from approval to success intent and 65 s for one conversion, but no log holds queue wait.

title: Continuation rules are written three times and differ between steps
summary: The step-to-family table exists in operations/index.ts, runtime.ts and packages/service/src/work.ts; hasMore means a different thing per step; recovery ignores two reports; comparisonId and the continue decoder are unused.

title: Operations for retired features still run in every pass
summary: expireHistoricalPreparations (no writer), comparison-publication and comparison-task resolvers (no producer), retireUnpinnedMainChecks (migration helper with an unbounded SELECT), and expireExports cost about 8 of 83 idle round trips.

title: Almost a quarter of operations/ source is reachable only from tests
summary: The archive writer in operations/history.ts and history-supplement.ts, copyVerifiedObject, putKnownLength, and reconcileWork have no production caller: about 1,130 of 4,824 lines.

title: The restore runbook names functions that have no runner
summary: sanitizeRestoredDatabase, inspectRecoveryImages and inspectRecoveryInventories are called only by tests; the check repair tool named in the incident record is not in the tree; the guide linked from every alert has no per-alert procedure.

title: Operational tables only grow; the capacity stop is the only brake
summary: No source DELETE exists for events, webhook receipts, pre-run checks, check creations, or status rows; operations_events has no secondary index and is fully scanned 29 to 129 times per pass; a capacity stop already blocked a real Submit on 2026-09-28.

title: The budget settings cover only part of the limits, and a deploy resets live overrides
summary: tasksPerStep is one knob read at 55 places while many limits are hardcoded outside the budget; the committed "{}" values replace any dashboard override at deploy; five preview variables are never read.

title: Alert kinds are free text; the Service view maps retired kinds and misses live ones
summary: Kinds are string literals in 14 files with four hand-written upserts; the view has texts for backup, backup-retention and comparison-publication but none for nine live kinds; retireSourceBaselines records no event on failure.

title: The operations guide does not match the code
summary: operations/README.md says the compare Worker consumes queue work, shows an unused comparisonId, and speaks of preview budgets; it is the linked recovery guide but has no step, alert, or cursor list.

title: Operation modules repeat the same plumbing in different ways
summary: The cursor upsert appears 11 times in 8 files and the empty report 13 times in 11 files; paging, clock source, assertion style, GitHub request helper, and project check each exist in two or three variants.

title: Each request that uses auth runs a full schema check against D1 first
summary: Better Auth 1.7.5 validates the schema for each new auth instance (sqlite_master select plus a 75-statement batch); createAuth runs for each request, so /api/me with no cookie takes 0.442 s median against 0.131 s for a path that exits before createAuth. validateSchema: false removes both calls (verified locally).

title: The Worker has no placement setting, so each D1 query and GitHub call is a long round trip
summary: No placement key and no cf-placement header; the Worker runs at the visitor edge (GRU) and D1 has no South America region, so the 3 or more sequential D1 calls and 2 to 3 GitHub calls of the access check each cost about 0.1 s. An explicit placement.region hint near D1 is the option; the D1 region is not verified.

title: The browser revalidates all hashed static files on each page load
summary: Production assets return cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate; the home page references 10 static files and apps/web/public has no _headers file. An /assets/* immutable rule removes the revalidation round trips.

title: A missing asset URL runs the full server render, and production deploys about 16 times each day
summary: An unknown /assets/*.js path returns an SSR HTML 404 (2,414 bytes, up to 1.45 s); with 67 production deploys in 4 days, open tabs can request chunks that no longer exist.

title: D1 read replication is not in use, and it gives little for the current users
summary: No withSession call exists, so all queries use the primary; replicas need the Sessions API and there is no South America region, so the gain for the current maintainer is small.

title: Deploy runs the full check suite again; 87% of deploy time is this second run, and superseded runs end as failures
summary: Deploy run 37357689984 took 433 s: 376 s for the repeated checks and 50 s for the deploy job; 9 of 78 push deploys failed at the 'current main commit' step because a newer commit superseded them.

title: Each push redeploys both Workers, and each change with a changeset causes a second CI and deploy cycle
summary: 43 of the last 120 main commits changed no deployable runtime file but each redeployed both Workers; private-package versioning adds a Version packages pull request (33 of 200 CI runs) and a second production deploy.

title: CI wall time went from about 210 s to about 294 s in 3 days; shards are unbalanced and old runs are not cancelled
summary: Vitest shard steps take 72 s to 292 s for the same commit, each shard pulls the Playwright image (26 s to 40 s) for 2 browser-dependent files, and checks.yml has no concurrency cancel for pull requests.

title: The normal deploy has no check after deploy, no version identity, and a weaker config guard than the manual path
summary: The push path ends at wrangler deploy; /health exposes no commit or version; deploy-source.mjs checks 3 config values while the manual path checks 19. Options: --tag, version_metadata binding, health check, wrangler rollback.

title: Each deploy depends on two retired queues and runs one-time cutover gates
summary: deploy-comparison-retirement.mjs reads two fixed legacy queue IDs and asserts response.ok on each production deploy; if the unused queues are deleted, all deploys fail. The container gate is now a no-op.

title: The production validator Worker has D1, R2, and queue bindings that its code does not use
summary: visonaut-compare binds the production DB, IMAGES, and OPERATIONS (deploy log), but apps/compare/src/index.ts reads no env; the Worker that decodes untrusted images has more access than it needs.

title: Production also answers on visonaut.ariakit.workers.dev
summary: workers_dev is true in env.production; the workers.dev host returns /health 200 and the full SSR shell 200, outside zone rules; the API returns 403 wrong_origin.

title: The raised CPU and subrequest limits apply to all handlers and to the preview Worker
summary: cpu_ms 240000 (8 times the default) and subrequests 250000 (25 times the default) are top-level, inherited by production, and present in the preview build; they date from the first commit and have no recorded reason.

title: The environment model (top level is preview, env.production is production) has specific risks
summary: Commands without an environment hit preview (safe), but production needs CLOUDFLARE_ENV at build and --env elsewhere, there is no local environment with bindings, 5 vars are duplicated, and every binding is optional in the generated Env type.

title: The public preview deploys only by manual dispatch and is behind main
summary: preview.visonaut.com serves older asset names (review-D6dKKXbW.css, index-CaJ_2b8I.css) while production serves the f83fef6 build (index-CXm4JU5N.css); preview deploys only through the preview-web dispatch.

title: Renovate is configured but has opened no pull request; pins are behind, and 8 release-age exclusions are stale
summary: 0 of 233 pull requests are from Renovate and there is no dashboard issue; wrangler is 4.136.1 against 4.147.0; all 8 minimumReleaseAgeExclude versions are about 14 days old against a 1-day default.

title: Version constants and resource identifiers are repeated by hand, and the compatibility date has 3 values
summary: Node 24.18.0 appears in 14 workflow lines, pnpm 12.5.1 in 13, the setup block 13 times; compatibility dates are 2026-09-21, -22, and -29, and the pinned workerd rejects 2026-09-29; the account ID is both a variable and a literal.

title: 20 TypeScript files are in no checked project, and the tsconfig files differ
summary: apps/web/tooling, apps/compare/test and container, packages/protocol/test, and root tooling are outside every include; typecheck:container is not run; two tsconfig files are unused; 5 of 8 projects do not extend the root file.

title: No version drift between workspaces, but some workspaces use dependencies that only the root declares
summary: 0 of 17 shared dependencies have two versions; apps/web, packages/service, packages/compare, and packages/cli use vitest, tsc6, @types/node, or @playwright/test from the root; the adapter pins engines to exactly 24.18.0.

title: Deploy guards are inline JavaScript in YAML, and tests cut them out with a regular expression
summary: Four node heredoc blocks in deploy.yml hold guard logic; release-guard tests extract them by regex and compile them; the largest guard repeats wrangler.jsonc values and runs only on manual actions.

title: Logs and traces use defaults only; there is no export and no alert from outside the service
summary: Workers Logs keep 7 days; there is no Logpush, Tail Worker, or uptime check; alerts live in the app's own D1 table and /health is static, so a dead Worker or D1 outage alerts nobody.

title: Several names no longer match what the thing does
summary: The 'compare' Worker, COMPARATOR binding, and README now only validate images; queues keep '-production-' while storage names lost it; routes differ in form; a legacy webhook path is still routed.

title: Small configuration items
summary: Stale changeset schema URL (3.1.1 against 4.0.1), Dockerfile digest without a tag (it is node:24.18.0-bookworm-slim), .infisical.json points to an undocumented dev project, pnpm check omits two CI commands, both deploy tokens are in one job environment, and other small items.

title: Better Auth validates the whole database schema on every request
summary: createAuth builds a new Better Auth instance per request (auth.ts:15-21, api/index.ts:130) and validateSchema defaults to true, so each request adds 2 D1 round trips, 76 statements (sqlite_master + 75 pragma_table_info) and ~856 rows read; ingest requests pay it too.

title: Every private request waits for 6 sequential D1 calls before its handler starts, and the review model needs 20
summary: Measured through handleApi: GET /api/runs 6 calls, /api/operations 9, /api/runs/:id 20 (sequential depth 15), /state poll 14, queued receipt 24; project, run and comparison rows are each read 3 times and readRunStatus is 6 awaits in a row.

title: Pull request titles are read from webhook payloads that the service has already erased
summary: webhooks.ts:330-335 sets payload_json='{}' after processing, but dashboard.ts:57-62 and review.ts:286-290 read $.pull_request.title from it; measured title 'Audit title' before processing and NULL after; index 0028 only holds NULL keys.

title: One status wakeup becomes a chain of queue messages that grows with the number of pull requests
summary: publishReviewLinks pages all PRs 25 per step and reports hasMore, and runtime.ts:454 re-sends the message; with 750 PRs an idle wakeup took 31 queue messages, 3,949 D1 calls and 7,597,795 rows read with zero work.

title: One review decision sends a new GitHub check update for every active run
summary: project.revision is one global counter (status-touch.ts:9-13) and checks.ts:200-209 treats every run with an older source_revision as stale; one decision caused 31 GET + 31 PATCH check-run requests and 740 extra D1 calls for 30 active runs.

title: The dashboard history query reads every comparison row in the database
summary: dashboard.ts:35-44 plan is SCAN row USING INDEX visonaut_rows_comparison plus a temp sort of all runs; 126,608 rows read for 100 runs shown, 18,214 with CROSS JOIN order, 12,312 with a (project_id, created_at) index; SELECT * also copies plan_json.

title: Recurring queue and cron statements scan whole tables; three of them are quadratic
summary: Closed-summary candidates (632,837 rows), staged-alert resolution (1,218,583) and statusRunEligibleSql (91,539 + 100,699) scan operations_events or snapshots per run; idle recovery step 921,542 rows read dropped to 91,798 with trial indexes and a rewritten predicate plan.

title: Lookups on request paths have no supporting index
summary: EXPLAIN shows SCAN for visonaut_checks by (project_id, external_run_id) on every decision (3,007 rows), visonaut_promotions by comparison_id, visonaut_audit by run_id, visonaut_status_outbox by run_id, and all project runs read per pull_request webhook.

title: The review-queue index from migration 0030 is not used; the queue poll reads every review task
summary: review-queue.ts:83-94 plans as SEARCH work_tasks_publication (kind=?) + temp sort, never work_tasks_review_queue; 1,501 rows read per poll with 1,500 completed tasks; adding state IN ('queued','leased') gives (kind=? AND state=?).

title: Many tables only grow, and admission stops new runs at 2 GiB
summary: No DELETE path for github_webhook_delivery (215 B/row measured), visonaut_status_outbox (149), pre_run_checks (667), work_checks, operations_events, ingest_staged_runs, ingest_review_sessions and others; capacity.ts rejects new runs above databaseAdmissionBytes = 2 GiB.

title: Each decision rebuilds and returns the complete review model
summary: The queued receipt (review.ts:812-833) calls reviewModel again: one decision on an 800-row comparison cost 49 D1 calls, 33,646 rows read and an 844 KB response although the command result already lists the changed revisions.

title: Image requests always reach the Worker, D1, and R2
summary: images.ts:24-40 does one D1 primary read and one R2 read per first view; the response is immutable but the Worker does not use the Cache API, so the edge never stores it.

title: Read replication cannot help yet: no Sessions API, and code depends on the raw binding object
summary: No withSession call exists and wrangler.jsonc has no placement key; the permission cache is a WeakMap keyed by the D1Database object (authorization.ts:19) and several flows read right after a write, so sessions need a bookmark plan.

title: Migration numbering has a duplicate and two gaps, and nothing checks it
summary: Two 0030_* files from PRs #190 and #198 (documented as kept), numbers 0017 and 0025 missing, and no test or CI script rejects a duplicate or out-of-order migration number.

title: Unused schema objects remain: 11 tables, 1 view, and 2 indexes
summary: Eight operations_backup_* tables, operations_promotions, transfer_key_redemptions, visonaut_baseline_restorations and view operations_ready_history_archives have no runtime reference in 169 source files; indexes work_tasks_review_queue and github_webhook_delivery_pr_title give no benefit.

title: Independent statements are sent one by one where one batch or one statement is enough
summary: An idle recovery step makes 385 D1 calls (60 are resolveEvents scans); persistWebhook is INSERT then SELECT, claimWork is two UPDATEs, operationsStatus is three independent reads, and review links run 4 statements per candidate (104 calls per page).

title: Wide rows and API bounds that can meet D1 limits
summary: Service.run uses SELECT * including plan_json (up to 1.5 MB) and is called up to 4 times per request; a command may carry up to 40,000 targets with 4 batch statements each and per-target JSON in one visonaut_commands row, which can pass the 2 MB value limit.

title: The dashboard requests its data only after JavaScript loads and hydrates
summary: SSR sends only 'Checking access and loading runs…'; /api/runs starts in useEffect after 602 kB of JS (564 ms at 150 ms/9 Mbps; production sign-in panel at 1,068 ms vs first paint 504 ms).

title: The run page requests the review model only after the entry JavaScript runs
summary: ssr: false plus a client loader makes HTML, scripts, model, render, and images sequential (model request 520 to 679 ms, first screenshot 814 ms at 150 ms/9 Mbps).

title: The header links and the Queue button are plain anchors, so each click reloads the document
summary: app-shell.tsx and review-workspace.tsx:580 use <a href>; each tab click is 1 document plus 11 more requests and a repeated access check, while the router Link to the same view needs 0.

title: Dashboard data lives in component state, so each mount and each refresh shows the loading text again
summary: No loader or cache for /api/runs; Back from a run and 'Refresh runs' blank the page to the loading text for the full API time.

title: Hashed static assets are served with max-age=0, must-revalidate
summary: Production and local both return 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' for /assets/*; there is no public/_headers, so each document load sends 9 to 10 conditional requests.

title: A click on a run gives no feedback for 1 second, and nothing is preloaded
summary: Default pendingMs of 1000 keeps the old page on screen until 1,123 ms after the click; no defaultPreload, and the 138 kB run chunk loads only after the click.

title: Each review action re-renders the whole workspace several times
summary: ArrowDown: 7 commits and 3,442 component renders of 1,121 mounted; approve: 10 to 12 commits, 64 to 80 ms keydown at 1x CPU and 256 to 264 ms at 4x; no memo or compiler.

title: The next screenshot is not preloaded
summary: Full images are requested only 26 to 29 ms after the key press; with 300 ms image latency each step waits 355 to 393 ms against 63 to 126 ms without it.

title: Tailwind compiles the stylesheet twice
summary: styles.css imports review.css and two TSX files import review.css again; 254 duplicate rules (128,286 bytes, 28%) stay in the 464,666-byte build file and dev injects two 371 kB style tags.

title: A large part of the stylesheet is for classes that the app never applies
summary: Up to 41.6% of unique utility bytes (123,735 of 297,711) belong to classes never seen in a broad session; unused vendored tabs and kbd recipes are scanned.

title: Class attributes dominate the markup
summary: 73% of the 28.5 kB loading-shell HTML is class attributes; a 100-run history table is 1.0 MB of markup with 874 kB of classes (1,683 bytes for each td).

title: Route chunks preload code that only a click needs
summary: The better-auth client (31 kB) and Popover plus Floating UI (53 kB) are preloaded on first load; sign-in and sign-out code is duplicated in three routes.

title: The Service status view waits for /api/runs before it requests /api/operations
summary: OperationsAttention mounts only when the run list is ready, so the service view and the header alert count need two sequential access-checked requests.

title: Operations polling does not stop when the tab is hidden
summary: operations-attention polls /api/operations every 60 s with no visibility check (1,440 requests for each tab for each day); the other two polls check visibility.

title: Build and dev hygiene: micro-chunks, misleading chunk names, heavy dev pages
summary: Three chunks of 199 to 474 bytes, a chunk named react that holds better-auth, and a dev page with 226 requests and 17.4 MB (lucide prebundle 5.4 MB).

title: The font stack names Inter Variable, but no font file ships
summary: ui.css names 'Inter Variable' but the build has 0 @font-face rules and no font file, so text differs between machines.

title: firefox.svg is 38 kB for a 16-pixel icon
summary: src/review/icons/firefox.svg is 38,092 bytes (10.5 kB gzip) and loads as a separate request; the other icons are 2 to 3 kB.

title: The service writes completed_at again on each re-send, so GitHub shows a wrong and growing duration and public data cannot show when a check first passed
summary: packages/security/src/checks.ts:197-200 sets completed_at to now on every delivery and every project event re-sends all eligible runs; one main check was read with completed_at 19:26:20Z, 21:20:31Z, then 21:37:03Z and the same conclusion; main median 'Submit end to completed_at' is 2 h 27 min 59 s (n=17), and 22 of 25 late writes follow another run's event.

title: A capacity pause refused Submit after the complete capture: 5 failed Submit steps in one afternoon, and two main commits keep a red check
summary: On 2026-10-04 from 11:31Z to at least 12:53Z (next success 21:32Z) POST /v1/runs answered capacity_exceeded after 14 to 17 minutes of CI each time; the check says only 'The pinned capture workflow ended with failure'; same incident type is on record for 2026-09-28; the cause (database size or 5 active runs) is not visible in public data.

title: One exact blob for each workflow file makes each consumer workflow edit a two-repository cutover; in two measured cutovers, 3 Submit jobs of other pull requests failed each time
summary: oidc.ts:87-92 and :171 accept one blob each and runtime.test.ts:122-124 forbids a second; 36 pin commits in 12 days, 5 service deployments for Ariakit #7703, 34 to 41 minute windows (n=4), 6 failed Submit jobs on 5 other pull requests; any edit of the 451 lines of ci.yml and app.yml (Renovate did 6 in app.yml before the pins) needs a service deployment; five options with the changed guarantee, none selected.

title: The same coupling value is written in two to four places, and one of them (the repository variable) carries no information
summary: Table of every value that must match (B, C, D, job names, CLI and adapter versions, protocol identities, Node, Playwright) with the checking code and the text the CLI prints; B exists in 4 places and the server compares VISONAUT_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_SHA only with its own value (workflow-owned.ts:297, :330-333), so begin can return it; decision needed only for the job-name env lines.

title: The executor digest D is a declared text, not a measured hash; nothing checks which adapter ran
summary: Ariakit app/playwright.config.ts:93,101 copies env VISONAUT_PACKAGE_SHA256 into the manifest, the adapter checks only the format (discovery.ts:84), the CLI and the server compare text with text, and no capture job step hashes the package; the value sits inside the file that pin B already fixes.

title: Six of eleven failed Submit steps print only 'The signed Submit check could not be started.'; three of them came 4 s to 3 min after the target branch moved
summary: Full table of the 11 failed Submit steps with log text, exit code, and cause; begin refuses for wrong pins, a superseded commit, or a merge ref that is not ready with the same sentence and exit 4; for a superseded main commit the server answers 503 with Retry-After for a permanent state (pre-run-attempts.ts:782-787), which matters for the PKG-01 option 'retry each 503'.

title: A commit has no Visonaut check for the first 15 minutes, and it never gets one when the capture fails or begin refuses
summary: The check is created inside begin (workflow-owned.ts:317): push to check exists is median 15 min 3 s, p90 25 min 48 s (n=48); pre-run-attempts.ts:971 settles only a check that exists, so 5 failed runs and 5 cancelled runs ended with no check on the head commit.

title: 22 of 78 checks (28%) link to the pull page that waits forever (incidence of API-03)
summary: All 22 'Visual capture is not required' checks keep details_url /pulls/<n>?check=... after completion (21 on the release pull request #7552), about 9 each day; this also confirms the API-03 assumption that GitHub keeps details_url when a PATCH omits it.

title: On main, 7 of 22 commits do not end with a passed check, and two checks are green with the title 'Visual review is running'
summary: Final main states: 15 passed, 2 red from the capacity pause, 1 red 'has not passed', 3 with no check (run cancelled by a newer push), 1 completed/success titled 'Visual review is running'; inferred cause: a pending intent after a success does not reopen a completed check on GitHub (not verified, needs a test write); no pull request path to that state was found.

title: A branch with an old copy of the workflow runs captures that cannot succeed: 9 runs and 1 h 34 min of capture jobs for one pull request, 0 checks
summary: Pull request #7694 targets solid-reboot, whose app.yml blob is the 2026-09-29 version; its capture jobs fail at 'Encrypt captures', and oidc.ts:299 accepts only base main anyway; this is consumer runner cost and a missing sentence in the consumer guide.

title: The adapter states an exact Node version that the consumer no longer uses, and the runbook repeats the old number
summary: packages/playwright/package.json:57-59 says node 24.18.0 exactly; after Ariakit #7744 the capture log shows node v24.21.0 and the runs pass, so nothing enforces it; docs/operations/adapter-service-pins.md:19 still says 24.18.0; the exact Playwright 1.63.0 peer means a Playwright patch in Ariakit needs an adapter release and a full pin cutover.

title: Firefox draws the stage background as triangles, not as a checkerboard
summary: screenshot-viewer.tsx:134 uses repeating-conic-gradient with oklch colors; Firefox 155 (headless and headed) matches a checkerboard at 77.5%, and adding `in srgb` gives 100% in all three engines.

title: `$layer="primary"` is near-white in Chrome and WebKit and near-black in Firefox (dark scheme)
summary: `primary` is not a theme color, so six main-action surfaces fall back to the system color `canvas`: #eeeeee in Chrome and WebKit, #28272e in Firefox dark (same in headed mode).

title: The native progress element ignores the brand color in all engines, and its colors differ by engine
summary: The preflight border disables the themed look, so `accent-brand` is dead: #008000 on #808080 in Chrome and WebKit, #0064b4 on #e6e6e6 in Firefox, in both schemes.

title: In WebKit, Tab skips all 13 links: the header nav, Queue, the item rows, and the variant chips
summary: Routed run page: 21 Tab stops and 0 links in WebKit against 34 stops and 13 links in Chrome (Option+Tab gives 34); an explicit tabindex="0" makes a link reachable.

title: Where a click puts focus differs: WORK-01 and A11Y-01 reproduce in Chrome and Firefox, and not in WebKit
summary: After a click on a variant chip, D, ArrowDown, and A do nothing in Chrome and Firefox; WebKit does not focus links and moves focus to the tabIndex=0 workspace root, so shortcuts keep working there by side effect.

title: A11Y-02 re-test: focus goes to the page root after each decision in all engines, and the ring on the root differs
summary: Approve and Undo move focus to the 1440 x 1014 root div in all three engines; the default ring is auto 1px in Chrome and auto 3px in Firefox and WebKit, and after a shortcut key only Chrome and WebKit show it.

title: In WebKit, Shift+Tab does not move focus after a mouse click on the label or the icon of a button
summary: Ariakit focuses the button in script, WebKit starts the backward search at the clicked child span, and the previous focusable element is the same button; a click on the padding or a plain native button does not show it. Likely upstream; not verified in real Safari.

title: Firefox find-as-you-type and quick find: a word runs commands, and a match in a chip stops all shortcuts
summary: Headed Firefox with typeaheadfind on: typing 'dialog' sets Difference, approves one variant, and sets Baseline; 'b' moves focus to the WebKit chip and then all shortcuts are ignored; with Shortcuts off the find works.

title: Firefox adds one Tab stop: the variant strip is a focusable scroll container
summary: The overflowing `nav` Variants is a Tab stop with the default engine ring in Firefox only (35 stops against 34).

title: Dates read differently in WebKit ("Oct 5, 2026 at 2:24 PM"), and columns shift
summary: toLocaleString(undefined, …) gives another pattern in WebKit; the history Created column is 10.4 px wider and 67 elements move.

title: Code text is SF Mono in WebKit and Menlo in Chrome and Firefox; the UI font is the same in all three
summary: Only WebKit resolves ui-monospace (2.7% wider hashes); no engine has Inter and all render San Francisco, with the h1 at 182.35 to 182.74 px (PRIM-16 holds everywhere).

title: The native select looks different in each engine, and a focus ring with no color is blue in Chrome and text-colored in Firefox and WebKit
summary: index.tsx:678 and :710 set outline width without a color; select height is 19, 17, and 20 px; A11Y-08 clipping and A11Y-09 underline-only focus are the same in all three engines.

title: Dark and light have different box sizes: `$border` is a 1 px border in dark and a ring in light
summary: ak-frame-bordering draws a real border only on dark layers: 14 elements on the queue and 12 on the workspace are 2 px larger in dark (Approve 34.5 against 32.5, strip 38 against 36, queue page 16 px taller), equal in all engines.

title: With classic scrollbars the item list cannot be opened from 1024 to 1038 px, and the variant strip grows by 15 px
summary: Confirmed A11Y-03 and SHELL-11 in headed Firefox with real classic scrollbars and with a 20 px root font in all three engines; the overflow-x strip also shows a permanent scrollbar (38 to 53 px).

title: The readiness gate accepts a truncated image in all engines
summary: With the first 40% of a PNG, decode() resolves and the size check passes in Chrome, Firefox, and WebKit; the state is ready and Approve is enabled on a partly drawn image.

title: Back and forward never use the page cache: the queue shows its loading text again, and view mode and zoom reset
summary: Cache-Control: no-store on documents (packages/security/src/http.ts:33) blocks the page cache in all three engines; Back sends the document and API requests again, and view mode and zoom return to Compare and Fit.

title: Headless Firefox moves the header underline away after an instant scrollTo (headless only)
summary: The fixed-position bar glider lands at rest position minus scrollY in headless Firefox only; headed Firefox, Chrome, and WebKit are correct. It is a capture caveat, not a user defect.

title: Design lab: pages load with no error in Firefox and WebKit, but the mask images differ, most in WebKit
summary: /primitives and /dev/fixtures have 0 errors and correct gliders in all engines; 35 of 56 masks match Chrome in Firefox and 21 of 56 in WebKit (page scene 3.25 times the red pixels).

title: Viewport and style do not reach the client. They exist only inside the cut key text, so 84 variants in 6 items have chips that read the same
summary: review.ts:469-482 builds the label from five fields and the key and never reads variant.dimensions; the key text gets 144 px of 317 px, and a dark-style preview chip says Light. Removing the key (COPY-04, WORK-24) would remove the only carrier of viewport and style.

title: Every item name is its key: a path of 23 to 68 characters. 62% of the characters repeat the family, and a list row takes three lines
summary: workflow-materialize.ts:334 falls back to the item key and the consumer passes no name; rows are 76 px with three name lines, 9 of 626 rows are visible, and the list is 44,714 px (65 screens).

title: The list is flat and in test-file order: 626 rows, 26 families, one "Accepted (626)" group, and "0 of 6 need review" on every row
summary: No grouping and no sort; a token change gives 41 rows that all read "6 of 6 need review" (2,601 px), and unchanged items are called Accepted.

title: Production has no thumbnails. Every row draws an empty "—" tile
summary: Only the retired server engine writes thumbnailImageId (apps/compare/src/process.ts:191-228); the local result has none, so the 26 px slot is a placeholder on every row (0 thumbnails in 40 captures).

title: A run with no changes opens as a full review workspace: the same image two times, four read-only statements, and a brand "Approve & next" button
summary: The observed run (626 accepted, archived) shows 186 words, "need review" 10 times, two copies of one image (reference and candidate are the same image object), and a decision bar with nothing to decide.

title: One status, superseded, covers four causes, and the UI says "A newer attempt replaced this comparison" for all of them
summary: review-status.ts:77 maps every closed run that is not accepted to superseded: new attempt, closed or merged pull request, expired failed run, retired baseline. A merged and approved pull request run can never read Passed.

title: 89% of production images are card crops that Fit shows at 100%. The picture covers a median of 24% of a Compare pane, and Fit cannot enlarge it
summary: 558 of 626 items render at scale 1; 51% cover less than a quarter of their pane; a zoom of 2 fits a Compare pane for 0 items but fits one full-width stage for 64.5%.

title: When only Firefox or Safari variants changed, the selected chip is off screen at load, and no other text names the browser
summary: In the browser regression scenario the selected chip (5 of 6) starts at 1,624 px in a 1,120 px strip (also off screen at 1920 px), scrollLeft is 0, and zero other text nodes name the browser.

title: A direct link to an item far down the list does not bring its row into view
summary: With 626 rows, the selected row is outside the list for 5 of 9 probed positions and cut for 1, also after 8 seconds; probable cause is one reveal against the 76 px row estimate while real rows are 60 to 92 px (cause not proved).

title: The search reads variant keys and labels, so a browser, scheme, or framework word matches almost every item
summary: item-list.tsx:46-54 searches keys and label parts: "safari" matches 568 of 626 items, "dark" 619 (4 have it in the name), "chrome" 626.

title: The pixel metric line is wrong or empty for four of the five variant kinds that production sends
summary: Added: "100.00% changed · 56,576 changed pixels"; removed: "— changed pixels"; a 2 px size change: "100.00% changed" plus "within the comparison tolerance"; unchanged: "0.00% changed · 0 changed pixels".

title: The design lab fixtures do not have the production shapes. A variant that works with them can fail with real data
summary: The lab large run has 120 items, 600 variants, human names, short keys, thumbnails, titles, a mask for size changes, and vector images; production has none of these shapes. Gap list in M11; replacement data in the scratch data folder.

title: A decision fails with 409 when any other write of the project commits at the same time
summary: Approve, Reject, and Undo assert the project revision and the run revision (review-commands.ts:213-216), so a commit on another row, run, or pull request gives 409 "State changed"; 17 of 40 concurrent decisions were lost locally, one overlap discards the queued chain, and the same guard makes the status `checks` step fail with a step-failed alert.

title: A Reject of a carried approval is dropped at the next push
summary: The reuse query (local-comparison.ts:24-36, :591) ignores a later rejection of the same tuple: approve in run 1, copy in run 2, Reject in run 2 by another reviewer, then run 3 with the same pixels is `approved/human(copied)` by the first reviewer and the check is `success`; this contradicts contract-issue-1.md:209.

title: A check that is locked after "success" keeps "success" after Reject or Undo
summary: After one failed GitHub read locks a check (OPS-01), a later Reject changes the service status to `rejected` but three healthy status passes send nothing, so the required check stays `success`; the lock blocks the fail-closed direction too.

title: A queued decision that fails 5 times is dead for its command ID, the 5 attempts take seconds, and a stopped consumer holds a decision for 12 minutes
summary: failWork retries with no delay (review-queue.ts:148-154), so a short storage fault makes the task `dead`; the receipt is 409 code `conflict`, the same ID again answers 202 and then 409 forever, no operations event is recorded, and the consumer's 12-minute lease delayed a decision to 721 s when the worker stopped.

title: The queued path and the direct path give different answers for the same refusal, and the queued path never names the reviewer
summary: The task result keeps only the error message (review-queue.ts:140-145), so the receipt has no `reviewer`, `incomplete` becomes `conflict`, a closed or promoted run answers the generic "State changed", and a missing predecessor answers 503 service_unavailable; review-guide.md:55 promises the reviewer name.

title: Two runs of one pull request can be open for review, and approvals on the older run are not carried
summary: reserveRun closes only attempts of the same workflow run (run-admission.ts:120-124); a new push leaves the older run open until the pull_request webhook retires it, and an approval saved there after the newer run is ready answers 200 but is not copied to the newer run.

title: "Equivalent merge check retired" makes the newest Visonaut check neutral also when the tested result failed
summary: pre-run-checks.ts:255-260 accepts a source check with conclusion `failure` and then writes `neutral` to the alias check on the same pull request head; GitHub counts `neutral` as passing, but which of two same-name check runs GitHub uses is not verified, and the path needs an unbound check row (old data or a stopped begin request).

title: A carried approval looks like a first-hand approval
summary: A copied decision keeps the kind and the actor of its source, and the review model returns only verdict, source `human`, and the first reviewer; no field says that the approval came from an earlier run, and the review guide has no sentence about carried approvals.

title: One command can have about 6,000 targets, and each target adds 4 statements and 2.4 KB to one batch
summary: 1,000 targets are 4,010 statements and 2.44 MB in one batch (114.5 ms locally), 5,000 targets are 20,010 statements and 12.2 MB (509.8 ms), both accepted by local D1; the 40,000 target limit cannot be reached because the 1 MiB body holds about 6,190 targets; the UI sends one item for each command today, so this matters for an "approve all" design.

title: Three "expected" fields of a decision command have no guard effect
summary: applyReviewCommand does not read expectedBaselineRevision or expectedPromotionId, and the route uses them and expectedRunRevision only to select the answer shape of the direct path; they are still part of the command identity for replay.

title: After a new sign-in, an open review tab cannot save again, and "Refresh current state" cannot repair it
summary: client.ts keeps one review-session promise; a new auth session makes every command answer 409 review_session_expired, shown as "Conflict. Start a new review session after signing in." until a browser reload (1 session request, same reviewSessionId on each retry).

title: An expired session during a review shows "Not saved. Sign in with GitHub." with no way to sign in, and "Refresh current state" then drops the decision
summary: The 401 text is plain server text, the workspace has no sign-in control, refresh() clears the held queue before the read, and a 401 on the receipt poll shows "Could not confirm…" instead of the cause.

title: The page says "You can close this window", but a queued decision that fails later is never shown, and a reload forgets each receipt
summary: Command IDs live only in React state and no endpoint lists a user's receipts, so after a close or reload pending decisions look undecided and failed ones leave no trace; this conflicts with docs/current-contract.md:196.

title: A queued decision that never completes shows the same line without end, and each queued decision polls 2 times each second with no bound
summary: Same text after 30 s (60 polls) and after 5 min (600 polls); one 500 ms loop per queued command, no backoff, no visibility pause, no elapsed time or link to Service status.

title: A newer push replaces the run under an open tab: the page finds out only when a save fails, uses four sentences for one cause, and has no link to the newer run
summary: No read between load and save; after the failed save four different texts say the run is over, ReviewModel has no successor field, and "Refresh current state" answers "Check the evidence before saving a new command." on a read-only run.

title: Decisions of another reviewer or another tab appear only after a failed save, and the conflict names the person by a numeric ID
summary: "Conflict. A target changed or belongs to another comparison. Updated by 5550002." prints the GitHub user ID (the user's own ID in the two-tab case), does not say which verdict was given, and offers a refresh that changes nothing visible.

title: A ready run page never reads again and has no refresh control; the queue never updates; no surface shows the age of its data
summary: staleTime Infinity with no refresh control outside error states; a dashboard hidden 10 minutes sends 10 alerts requests and 0 run-list requests, reads nothing on return, and shows no age text.

title: The client ignores error.code: each 409 is "Conflict", each 403 is "write access", each other error is "Not saved" or "temporarily unavailable"
summary: Three call sites map the HTTP status differently and none reads the code; 29 of 103 realistic matrix cells name the wrong cause and 33 have no way forward.

title: The three "no access" screens differ, and two are dead ends
summary: Dashboard has Retry and Use another account, pull page only Use another account, run page only Retry and no account menu; on a wrong origin Use another account fails with "Sign-out failed."

title: When a background poll gets a 401, the dashboard silently becomes the public landing page
summary: The queue or history is replaced by "Every change. A clear decision." with no session-ended text, no live-region entry, lost search state, and focus on body.

title: Offline: no automatic retry for saves or images, the browser's raw error text, and no connection state
summary: "Not saved. Failed to fetch"; 0 requests in 5 s after the connection returns; no online listener; blocked A/X keys give only a screen-reader-only line.

title: A click on a run while offline replaces the app with the browser's offline page
summary: The router treats any failed chunk import as deploy skew and reloads the document, so an offline click on a not-yet-loaded route ends on chrome-error with ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED.

title: A chunk that stays missing after the automatic reload ends in the router's bare "Something went wrong!" screen
summary: A single missing chunk is fixed by a silent reload, but a second failure shows TanStack's default error with the module URL and no shell; the run route's own error component is a lazy chunk too, and there is no defaultErrorComponent.

title: A tab cannot detect a deploy, and an API format change gives messages that hide the cause and a button that cannot help
summary: No build ID on responses or /health; a newer model format shows "Could not confirm…" then "Not saved. This review format has changed. Refresh before reviewing." although the server saved the decision, and only "Refresh current state" is offered.

title: A 5xx answer that is not JSON tells the user to check the connection; the maintenance text and its Retry-After: 60 are dropped
summary: The cutover-fence 503 text answer shows "The service did not return review data. Check your connection and refresh." on the run page and on saves.

title: 503 handling differs on each surface: the reference is dropped on five of ten, Retry-After is never read, and the retry policy is one of four
summary: Queue, history, service page, bell, and pull page drop the server message and reference; retries are none, fixed 2 s, fixed 60 s, or stop; no client code reads Retry-After: 1.

title: The Service status page cannot open while /api/runs fails
summary: The status view renders only after the run list is ready, so a run-list 503 shows "The review queue could not be loaded" under the Service status tab with 0 requests to /api/operations.

title: Permanent states offer "Retry", and evidence errors offer nothing
summary: An unknown run (409 incomplete) and a missing check offer only Retry; an image 404 says "Check your connection"; a dimension mismatch has no control because recompareAllowed is always false.

title: A sign-in that fails at GitHub leaves the app: the user gets Better Auth's default error page, or the landing page with no message, and the deep link is lost
summary: Sign-in passes no errorCallbackURL and auth.ts sets no onAPIError; a cancel, an expired state (10 min), or a failed code exchange redirects to /api/auth/error, which renders a foreign page with an "Ask AI" link or redirects to /?error= that the landing page ignores (branch depends on NODE_ENV; not verified on production).

title: The auth rate limit answers 429 after three sign-in starts in 10 seconds; the page says "could not start, try again" and enables the button at once
summary: Better Auth's built-in /sign-in rule is 3 per 10 s with X-Retry-After: 10; the three sign-in surfaces and sign-out show a generic failure, ignore the wait, and the pull page swaps to "Review unavailable".

title: A historical comparison is marked by one unstyled sentence; counts and badges still say "need review", and the decision keys do nothing with no feedback
summary: Only a plain line and 10 px header text mark the read-only view; "9 of 11 need review" and a filled Approve button remain; key A gives no request, text, or announcement; the current comparison has no visible mark in Details.

title: Recovery moves focus to body, alerts read their button labels as text, and one blocking message exists only for screen readers
summary: Focus is on body after Retry, after Refresh current state, and after a session end; the bar's live text is "Not saved. Failed to fetchRetry same commandRefresh current state"; the 'resolve first' message is sr-only.

title: After a sign-out in another tab, an open run page keeps its content and all its controls
summary: No cross-tab signal; the run stays on screen with 0 requests until a navigation or a save fails; Back to the queue and Forward to the run then show the sign-in screens.

title: The real run inventory uses 72.9% of its 16 MiB write limit; at about 5,260 captures each Submit fails
summary: The inventory for the real 3,832-capture set is 11.66 MB (3,043 bytes for each capture, 60% is the embedded manifest); writeCaptureInventory throws at 16 MiB, which is about 5,500 captures, below the 10,580 that the contract plans for.

title: One Submit reads and validates the complete reference inventory at least 27 times
summary: Each of the 20 reference pages, three validations, and two input reads downloads and validates the same immutable 11.5 MB object again (about 310 MB for each run); the count for each call is measured, the total is computed, and the production time share is not measured.

title: inherited-by pins form a chain, so replaced baseline images and the imported baseline do not expire after 30 days
summary: An inherited-by pin is released only when the borrowing run's bytes are deleted, so each retained main run holds all owners that its inventory named; in the probe the imported image stayed stored and public after three later baselines had replaced it.

title: After a D1 restore, objects written after the restore point have no row, no check finds them, and no step deletes them
summary: In a modeled 24-hour rewind, inspectRecoveryImages found the three rows that point to deleted objects and the ordinary passes repaired them, but four objects of runs created in the window stayed with no row forever; the recovery code has no list call, does not read QUARANTINE, and does not check masks.

title: The QUARANTINE bucket no longer holds images; facts and options for the two-bucket rule (S01, D16)
summary: Uploads go directly to IMAGES with only a size and SHA-256 check, QUARANTINE gets only the staged manifest and plan evidence, nothing moves between the buckets, and private inventories live in IMAGES; five options are listed and none is selected.

title: The full operations pass and most retention steps have no test on runs with an inventory
summary: By script census, runOperations has 0 of 6 tests with an inventory run, expireRunImages 3 of 12, expireComparisonReferences 0 of 2, and sanitizeRestoredDatabase 0 of 21; the sparse fixture uses an old-form baseline except in one test, and production first runs these paths about 30 days after the cutover.

title: No code deletes run inventories: 11.7 MB for each run, about 5 to 8 GB each month, and the key layout prevents a prefix rule
summary: Each service run (estimate 450 to 680 each month from four days of CI data) leaves one 11.66 MB inventory forever; the price is about 1.27 USD each month after one year, gzip makes the object 8 times smaller, and inventories share the runs/<run>/ prefix with deletable images.

title: 25 candidates that cannot be deleted stop all later image deletions
summary: expireRunImages has no cursor and skips an unsafe-prefix candidate without a state change, so 25 such rows fill each page; in the probe a normal run behind them was never deleted over six cron ticks and the step reported hasMore false.

title: Plan evidence in QUARANTINE has no reader and no deleter, and ingest_manifests.object_key points to an object that is deleted after one day
summary: Each run writes plans/workflow/<digest>.json (545 bytes) that only test-reachable code reads and no prefix delete covers, and the staged manifest key stored in ingest_manifests is deleted with the stage after about 24 hours.

title: On the sparse path the reuse endpoint handles only changed images; an unchanged run costs no image operation
summary: Unchanged captures are not staged, so an unchanged full run has 0 image puts, gets, and reuse copies; reuse now copies only changed images uploaded in the last day by another run, and the copy is necessary only because a changed capture must be owned by its run.

title: A closed summary hides images that still exist, and the expired flag looks only at the run's own bytes
summary: 30 days after close, also for the current baseline, the page shows a text box while all image URLs in the model return 200; imagesExpired stays false when reference images of other owners return 404, and a proposed UI text says the images are deleted.

title: All Better Auth routes are served, and a session of any account that can sign in is sufficient for them
summary: server.ts passes all of /api/auth/* to Better Auth; with a session cookie, refresh-token and get-access-token return GitHub user tokens in plain text, account-info proxies GitHub, update-user writes the profile, and each sign-in of any GitHub account stores user, account, session, and audit rows. Correction of revision r9: not each GitHub account can sign in. The sign-in App is private, so only the members of the organization can (a GitHub rule that nobody tested).

title: A signed-in account without repository access causes 2 GitHub App requests on each private request
summary: A refused user costs 5 D1 round trips and 2 installation-token requests on each request, with no negative cache and no rate limit, so one outside account can use up the App rate budget that the required Visonaut check depends on. Correction of revision r9: the account is not an outside account. It is a member of the organization without push permission, or a person who lost access and kept a session.

title: Pull request code selects the comparison settings, and the loosest settings make each change unchanged
summary: The capture manifest carries threshold, maxDiffPixels, and maxDiffPixelRatio with no service-side limit; threshold 1 made an all-black image unchanged against an all-white one, and unchanged captures create no review row, so the check passes with no review.

title: On main, new and removed identities reach the baseline with no human decision and no upper bound
summary: Automatic acceptance of introductions and removals is a contract rule and the only path from capture output to the baseline without a person; a main run that captures too few tests removes the rest of the baseline with a passed check.

title: The ingest capability renews itself without OIDC, also after Submit
summary: Each answer of POST /v1/runs/:id/reference contains a new 600-second capability and the route does not check submitted_at; a chain of 17 calls stayed valid for 154 minutes and kept read access to the baseline inventory.

title: An OIDC token is accepted again inside its 10 minutes, and one audience serves three endpoints
summary: jti is required but never stored, Begin, Reserve, and Submit share the audience <origin>/submit, and environment and runner_environment are not checked; a replay of Reserve returns a new capability.

title: The Submit job installs the CLI by version only, the saved consumer patch shows a digest check that is not live, and the pinned blobs use action tags
summary: The live app.yml runs pnpm add visonaut@0.5.4 with no archive digest check while docs/operations/ariakit-consumer.patch shows curl plus sha256sum, and the blob pin does not fix the code behind actions/*@v7 tags.

title: A fork pull request never gets the required Visonaut check, and only the saved contract says so
summary: pre-run-candidates.ts and oidc.ts refuse a head repository other than ariakit/ariakit, so a fork pull request cannot satisfy the branch rule; 0 of the last 400 consumer pull requests came from a fork.

title: A signed webhook body is accepted again under a new delivery ID
summary: The delivery ID and event name are unsigned headers, so a captured revocation body with a new GUID signed the user out a second time; the alias URL /webhooks/github is still live.

title: Ingest routes do database work, and one outbound request, before they check the credential
summary: Anonymous POST /v1/runs/:n/submit answers 401 or 404 by staged-run existence after 3 to 5 round trips, a forged bearer starts a JWKS fetch, and a bad percent sequence in a shard path gives 503 plus an operation-failed log line.

title: There is no procedure to rotate a secret outside database recovery
summary: The five runtime secrets each have one accepted value and rotation is described only as a step of database recovery, so the effects of a change during an incident are not written down.

title: Each model read validates two 12 MB inventories again; this is 84 to 95% of the request time on a local machine
summary: readCaptureInventoryDocument repeats the canonical check, two manifest parses, 21,678 profile digests, and the receipt check on each read; keeping only the digest check cuts the request from 696 ms to 158 ms in workerd (870 to 129 ms in Node) with the same response bytes.

title: About 3.0 to 3.7 s of the production wait is not split yet: 24.3 MB from R2 in two sequential reads, and the speed of a Workers core
summary: Bytes, sequence, and local CPU are measured; the production split is not. One invocation log or trace (CPU time, R2 spans) decides between compressing the inventory (12.15 MB becomes 1.5 MB gzip) and the CPU fix of WAIT-01.

title: The first response carries 3,828 unchanged variants to show 4 changed ones: 5.33 MB against 7.5 KB
summary: With only the rows that D1 stores, the response is 7,483 bytes with 0 R2 reads and 8 D1 calls, but the changed rows have no reference image because that link is only in the baseline inventory; contract line 26 and decision P01 require the complete model today.

title: Almost each capture has its own profile, because the clip rectangle is part of the profile
summary: The real run has 3,613 profiles for 3,832 captures (81 without the clip); profiles are 47% of the manifest, 22% of each inventory, 1.3 MB of the model, and the source of the 21,678 digests for each model read.

title: A run with more than about 5,270 captures cannot be stored (1.38 times today), and the limits do not agree
summary: writeCaptureInventory throws at 5,326 captures (16 MiB) while the CLI accepts about 5,700 and maximumCaptures is 40,000; by code reading the error is an hourly retry with a generic alert, not a named failure (that path was not run).

title: Three model reads at the same time need 105 to 109 MB of live JavaScript heap at today's size; the isolate limit is 128 MB
summary: V8 heap caps in Node: one read completes at 56 MiB, two at 88, three at 112; receipts can overlap by design (client.ts:306), and sha256() copies each 12 MB buffer; hosted accounting is not measured.

title: A run with a closed summary still reads both inventories from R2, and its response is the largest
summary: For detail_archived = 1 the request still makes 2 R2 reads of 24.3 MB (14 D1 calls, 12 in sequence) and returns 6.35 MB, because one 106-character reason is repeated two times for each variant; the comment at closed-summary.ts:20 says the API reads only D1.

title: After 10 s or more with no request, the first Worker request on a new connection waits about 0.2 s more in 70% of the samples; Cloudflare reports the time before the Worker code runs
summary: 45 samples: cold /health is over 100 ms slower in 1 of 8 at 1 s, 4 of 9 at 10 s, 7 of 9 at 60 s, 6 of 9 at 300 s, 7 of 8 at 900 s (median 185 ms, p90 268 ms when slow), all as cfEdge with cfWorker 0 to 1 ms; the asset and D1 are not the cause, and no sample was within 10 minutes of a deploy.

title: The size of the stylesheet is not the cause of the slow lab; the work that its rules give to the browser is
measured: 42% to 71% of the main thread time of a page
summary: Chrome parses the 475 KB sheet in 5 to 13 ms and a sheet of double size changes nothing; with an empty sheet the main thread work of one page goes down by 42% to 71% in the production form. Three checkers do not agree on the cost of rules that match no element (0 to about 40% of the style time).

title: The live frames of the lab gallery are 10 full apps in one page
measured: 3.8 to 5.1 s against 0.9 to 1.1 s on a development server, with 10 frames
summary: The gallery of the lab of revision r7 had 10 live frames, and the directions page 6. On a development server of a copy (load average 28 to 58): 3,185 requests and a quiet main thread after 3.8 to 5.1 s, against 223 requests and 0.9 to 1.1 s with the frame documents blocked. In the production form: 846 requests and a quiet network after 2.2 s, against 71 requests and 0.7 s. The earlier lanes measured 9 to 19 s against about 1 s for the lab of round 2 (15 frames, load average 12 to 850). The real app is one document, so it does not have this cost. Changed in r8 (D-PERF-03): the gallery and the directions page of the lab show one picture for each card, and the page explorer keeps its live frame. Lab round 4 measured 222 requests for the gallery on a development server, where it measured 3,191 with live frames, and 69 in the production form, where it measured 847. The independent review of the round measured 222 and 69, where it measured 3,187 and 848.

title: The hover glider of a nav makes one key press recalculate the whole list
measured: 1,217 of 1,734 elements in one recalculation; 70 with the bar glider only
summary: The two hover rules of navGlider have `.nav:not(:has(...)) > &`, so the nav is the anchor of a `:has()` that is not in the subject, and with the rule shape of PERF-04 Chrome recalculates its subtree at each change inside it. Arrow key at 41 rows: 80 ms to the next frame with the four gliders of the lab of revision r7 and 36 ms with the bar glider only; pointer over 6 rows: 483 ms and 24 ms of style and layout. A rewrite of the two rules with the `:has()` in the subject gives 72 elements with four gliders and equal pictures; it ran in a copy of the lab only. The hover rules of a glider group (glider.ts:113 and :117) have the same form and were not measured. Changed in r8 (D-PERF-01): the screenshot list of the lab has the bar glider only, and lab round 4 measured 69 and 70 elements for an arrow key in the built lab, where it was 1,216 and 1,217. The independent review of the round measured 66 to 122 on different rows, where it was 1,216 to 1,234. The page links of the header and the run rows of the Queue and of History keep a hover glider, and nobody measured them.

title: Ten recipe class names make a `:has()` rule shape that lets each `:has()` anchor recalculate its whole subtree
measured: 1,217 against 155 recalculated elements for one arrow key
summary: A compound with `:has()`, then a combinator, then `*` (also inside `:is()` or `:not()`) puts 'the whole subtree' into the one invalidation set that Chrome keeps for `:has()` outside the subject. The lab sheet has 23 such rules, from `ui-disabled-within`, `ui-field-disabled`, `ui-choice-on`, and `ui-choice-disabled` with `**:`, `*:`, `group-.../name:`, and `not-...:`; the copy of apps/web has 2 of the class names (control.ts:317 and :322). Two anchors were measured: the nav with a hover glider (PERF-03), and the Shell root, where one element that is added to the main panel recalculates 1,546 of 1,636 elements, and 124 without the 10 class names. The removal of the 10 class names is a test: it changes disabled and checked choice controls. Nobody tested a rewrite.

title: Three recipe class names make a sibling rule shape: an element that is added or removed before a sibling recalculates the subtree of its parent
measured: 2,435 of 2,589 elements for an arrow key that removes tooltips; 85 without the 3 rules
summary: `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:outline-none`, `not-ui-sibling-selected:hidden`, and `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:invisible` compile to `X ~ *` where an alternative of X is only a pseudo-class (`:focus-visible`, `:checked`). With one of the 3 rules in the sheet, Chrome recalculates the subtree of a parent when a child is added or removed before a sibling: 1,637 elements for one empty element before the last child of the body at 41 rows, 96 with the rewrite, and 94 for an element that is added as the last child. Ariakit removes the portal node of a tooltip from the body, so an arrow key recalculates the document when the variant control makes new tooltips: 8 of the first 60 arrow keys with each folder open (335 ms against 136 ms with the rewrite). A rewrite of two custom variants (`ui-focus-visible` as a selector list, `:checked:where(.control)` in `ui-sibling-selected`) changes 63 selectors and no declaration, adds 6,646 bytes, and gives equal pictures; it ran in a copy of the lab only. The built sheet of apps/web has the 3 rules.

title: The variant control of the settled design makes new tooltips for each screenshot
measured: 3 children of the body removed and 3 added for one arrow key
summary: `VariantPager` gives each mark the key of its variant, so a screenshot with other variant keys removes each `Hint` and adds a new one, and each tooltip has a portal node in the body. With PERF-05 this is one recalculation of the document: in the fixture, 8 of the first 60 arrow keys with each folder open (335 ms to the next frame against 110 ms for the other 52 keys). With the key of the place, no key of the 60 recalculates the document: 15 to 67 elements for 58 keys, and 121 and 321 for the 2 keys that add a tooltip. No key of the 60 removed a tooltip, and a removal can still cost the document until Ariakit UI has the rewrite.

title: The style cost for each element is the formulas of `ak-layer`; the typed registered properties of @ariakit/tailwind limit it
measured: about 170 µs for one element with ak-layer at a full recalculation; 2 µs for an element with no class
summary: One element with `ak-layer` costs about 170 µs at a full recalculation when Chrome cannot reuse a computed style, and an element with no class 2 µs; 1,000 equal siblings with `ak-layer` cost 1.6 µs each. The review page has 522 such elements in 1,731, and one full recalculation costs 84 ms (52 µs for each element). The typed rules are not the cost: with `syntax: "*"` a full recalculation is 15 times slower for the 14 colors and 6 times for the 11 lengths; for the 26 numbers the picture is equal and the time is 5% more; with `inherits: true` on the 32 rules that have `false`, 3% of the pixels differ. Without the 51 rules the time is 65% less and 83% of the pixels differ. 330 style queries of the package read 6 of the colors, 1 number, and 1 length, so these need their type. No faster form with an equal picture was found, and which formula costs how much is not known.

title: Rows rendered in parts do not help at 41 rows and help at 585 rows only after the rewrite of PERF-05
measured: 128 ms against 55 ms for the arrow key at 585 rows, after the rewrite of PERF-05
summary: `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-block-size` on each row, added in the browser. At 41 rows the arrow key is equal with the bar glider only (34 and 32 ms), and 10 wheel steps cost 199 ms against 57 ms (101 layouts against 19). At 585 rows it does not remove the recalculation of PERF-05 (1,905 of 2,590 elements), and after that rewrite it cuts the arrow key from 128 ms to 55 ms, with 515 ms against 339 ms for the wheel. 30 arrow keys keep the focus, the scroll place, and the bar; the accessibility tree of Chrome keeps each row (593 links); `innerText` of a row that is not rendered is empty. A window of visible rows was not built.

title: With the CPU slowed 4 times, the arrow key of the settled review page needs 344 ms as built and 134 ms with the bar glider only, and Approve stays near 200 ms
measured: 344 ms as built, 134 ms with the bar glider only (load average 3 to 12)
summary: 41 rows, production form, 5 runs in turns at a load average of 3 to 12. Arrow key to the next frame: 344 ms as built, 134 ms with the bar glider only, and 126 to 160 ms for the three other forms with no cost of the hover glider. Approve: 425 ms as built and 196 to 218 ms for the four other forms. Script is 126 to 146 ms of each arrow key in each form (31 to 36 ms with no throttle), so after the glider choice script is the larger part. At a load average of 33 to 44 the same builds needed 450 to 481 ms and 184 to 232 ms for the arrow key, and the research runs at 22 to 78 gave 438 to 515 ms and 188 to 276 ms: no time is the time of a quiet machine. In this finding, “as built” is the lab of revision r7, with four gliders. Changed in r8 (D-PERF-01): the lab has the bar glider only, and lab round 4 measured 132 ms for the arrow key and 201 ms for Approve in the built lab with the CPU slowed 4 times, where they were 335 ms and 408 ms (load average 5.4 to 10.9). The independent review of the round measured 131 ms and 189 ms, where they were 331 ms and 404 ms (load average 4.3 to 6.1), and 193 ms and 300 ms, where they were 523 ms and 599 ms, at a load average of 54 to 103.

title: The development server multiplies the script time of an interaction by 3.8 to 5.7
summary: React development mode with StrictMode, and unbundled modules: one preview is 363 requests and about 20 MB in development against 104 requests in the production form. Style and layout are equal in both forms. Judge the speed of a design in the production form: `vite build`, then `vite preview`.
